    Before you fly

    • Fill in the free TDAC arrival card in the 3 days before you land, only on tdac.immigration.go.th.
    • Install and set up the must-have apps while your home SIM still gets the SMS codes.
    • Book the Samui flights for 19 and 23 Jan, and a room in Ban Tai for full-moon week.
    • Buy party tickets early: the cheaper tiers sell out (Argy: presale from Tue 20 Oct, 18:00 Thai time).
    • Leave vapes and e-cigarettes at home: they are illegal in Thailand.
    • Check your passport: valid at least 6 months after arrival, with a free page.

      8–26 Jan 2027 · underground first

      Music & raves

      Phuket's party scene is mostly beach clubs with big-name DJs. The most underground nights are small and announced late: Shelter in Patong and the crews at Courage Bar in Old Town. For proper jungle raves, go to Koh Phangan: a 1-hour flight to Samui plus a boat. In full-moon week (19 to 23 Jan) it has a party every night.

      A plan for your 18 nights

      Group · 8–18 Jan

      • Fri 8 Jan: arrive. Argy at Café del Mar in Kamala from 14:00, or Shelter at Illuzion in Patong from 23:30.
      • Sat 9 Jan: Circoloco at Baba Beach Club Natai, 15:00 to 03:00. Book a driver both ways: about 1 hour from Kamala.
      • Sun 10 to Wed 13 Jan (morning): Koh Phangan with the group. Lost Jungle (Parvati Day & Night) runs until 11 Jan, Chill Up on Monday, the Lighthouse Party on Tuesday.
      • Going to Koh Phangan only once? Make it the full-moon week (19 to 23 Jan), and use 10 to 13 Jan for boat trips and the Enthusiast Place open doors (Tue 12).
      • Wed 13 Jan: Marco Carola at Café del Mar. Fly back in the morning if you are on Koh Phangan.
      • Fri 15 Jan: Shelter again, or whatever the Courage Bar crews (SUB, FAKE PALM, Enthusiast) have on.
      • Sat 16 Jan: Circoloco, second weekend. Mon 18 Jan: the group leaves.

      Two of you · 19–23 Jan

      • Tue 19 Jan: fly to Koh Samui (the 14:15 flight or earlier), then the boat to Thong Sala. Stay in Ban Tai. Tonight: OXA (moved to Tuesday this week) or the Lighthouse Party.
      • Wed 20 Jan: Waterfall (expected). Thu 21 Jan: Jungle Experience (expected), with Chill Up as the warm-up.
      • Fri 22 Jan: the Full Moon Party on Haad Rin. Bring cash and closed shoes, and leave your passport in the safe.
      • Sat 23 Jan: boat to Samui at 10:30 or 11:00, then the 15:05 flight. You land at 16:05 and reach Circoloco in Natai at about 17:00, for the last weekend. Book this flight now.
      • Staying in Phuket instead? Enthusiast Place on Tue 19, Shelter and DnB Allstars (Chalong, 22 to 24 Jan) on Fri 22, Circoloco on Sat 23.

      Solo · 24–26 Jan

      • Base: near the airport in Nai Yang (5 to 10 minutes to the terminal), or a social hostel in Patong if you want company.
      • Sun 24 Jan: the Sunday Walking Street market in Old Town (16:00 to 22:00), or a beach day.
      • Mon 25 Jan: last party night. Open on Mondays: Illuzion, BOA and Armania in Patong, and Levitate (to 01:00). Closed: Shelter, Courage Bar and the Café del Mar Club Room.
      • Tue 26 Jan: check out, leave your bags, lunch at Natural Restaurant or on Nai Yang Beach, then plane spotting or the 13:30 Soi Dog tour. Be at the airport by 15:20 for the 18:20 flight.

      Lighthouse Party (Haad Rin)

      Lighthouse Bungalows, Haad Rin, Koh Phangan · Koh Phangan

      Fri 8Tue 12Fri 15Tue 19
      Underground 4/5

      Techno party on the rocks at the end of Leela Beach, Haad Rin. You walk along the beach and over a bridge above the sea. Local and international DJs play deep house, techno and progressive until sunrise. Tuesdays all year, Fridays too in high season. Smaller and more underground than the Full Moon Party.

      technodeep houseprogressive house
      When
      Every Tuesday all year; Fridays too in high season (every Friday from 19 Dec 2025 to 3 Apr 2026). When the Full Moon Party falls on a party night, the Lighthouse moves (Mon 2 Mar 2026 instead of Tue 3 Mar).
      Tickets
      Free early. Recent listings (Mar and Oct 2026): free before 22:00. The phangan.events guide: free before 21:00, 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) from 21:00 to 22:00, 600 THB (≈6,500 AMD) after 22:00.
      Line-up, tips & links
      Type
      weekly night
      • Tue 19 Jan is the safe date this week. Fri 22 Jan is Full Moon night, so the Friday party may move or skip. Check the listing that week.
      • Wear shoes with grip. The path and rocks can be wet and dark.
      • Shared taxis run from about 20:00 from all main beaches. Just say 'Lighthouse'.
      • Koh Phangan is far from Phuket. The fastest way is a flight to Koh Samui, then a boat. Plan at least 2 nights.

      Shelter Phuket (small club room inside Illuzion)

      Shelter Phuket, 31 Bangla Road, Patong (behind the Illuzion main stage) · Patong & Kalim

      Fri 8Sat 9Fri 15Sat 16Fri 22Sat 23
      Underground 3/5

      Small club room behind the Illuzion main stage on Bangla Road, for about 500 people, with a Funktion-One sound system. Resident and guest DJs play house, tech house, minimal and some techno, mostly on Fridays and Saturdays. Not a Berlin-style club, but the most music-focused room in Patong.

      housetech houseminimaltechno
      When
      Most Fridays and Saturdays, usually 23:30 to 04:00. In your dates: Fri 8, Sat 9, Fri 15, Sat 16, Fri 22 and Sat 23 Jan. Check the line-up first: some weekends have no Shelter night.
      Tickets
      500 THB (≈5,400 AMD) for Oct 2026 nights (illuzionphuket.com). VIP tables cost extra.
      Line-up, tips & links
      Type
      club
      • You enter through Illuzion. Bring your passport (20+). Smart casual, no flip-flops or beachwear.
      • Check the line-up on illuzionphuket.com/events or Instagram @shelter_phuket before you go.
      • Local crews sometimes host showcase nights here, for example Enthusiast with Cosmjn (Jun 2026). These are the best nights for deeper sounds.

      Parvati Day & Night at Lost Jungle

      Lost Jungle (new hilltop jungle site, Koh Phangan; address not public) · Koh Phangan

      Sat 9Sun 10Mon 11
      Underground 4/5

      A Parvati Records party by Sacred Moon Phangan: about 48 hours of non-stop forest and dark psytrance in the Koh Phangan jungle. It is also the opening of Lost Jungle, a new hilltop site with camping, art market and food. With Giuseppe, Atriohm, Ectogasmics, Kerlivin and more. Not techno.

      psytranceforestdarkpsy
      When
      Sat 9 to Mon 11 Jan, about 48 hours non-stop. Start time not final (ticket shop: Sat 4 PM; phangan.events: Sat noon)
      Where
      Exact place not public yet. Check the organiser before you go.
      Tickets
      2,500 THB (≈27,000 AMD) on the organiser's Vibez shop (second advance tier from 17 Oct 2026; first tier was 2,000 THB, ≈21,600 AMD)
      Line-up, tips & links
      Lineup
      Atriohm, Giuseppe, Ectogasmics, Obelisk, Weirdos, Audiofools, Ectobot, Gu, Kerlivin, KT, Aztec Dosage, Alien Trancesistor, Makumba, Kokobloko, Slate, Capodanna, Kia Goa, Manousakiz
      Type
      festival
      • The exact location is not public yet. Ask Sacred Moon Phangan or check phangan.events before you go. The map pin is only the island centre.
      • Google Maps has no 'Lost Jungle' yet. The search shows Retro Mountain club instead. Do not go there without checking.
      • It clashes with Circoloco on Sat 9 Jan.
      • From Phuket: fly to Koh Samui (about 1 h), then boat to Koh Phangan (30-60 min). There is a camping area on site.

      Circoloco Thailand 2027

      Baba Beach Club Natai (Baba Beach Jungle) · Natai & Khao Pilai (Phang Nga)

      Sat 9Sat 16Sat 23
      Underground 3/5

      The famous Monday party from DC-10 Ibiza, on Natai Beach north of Phuket. Three Saturdays (9, 16 and 23 Jan), 3 PM to 3 AM, from sunny afternoon to night by the sea. House, tech house and some techno. Sat 23 Jan is the last one. The 2027 lineup is not out yet. In 2026: Michael Bibi, Palms Trax, Adriatique.

      housetech housetechno
      When
      Sat 9, Sat 16 and Sat 23 Jan, 3 PM - 3 AM each day
      Tickets
      Dice: from EUR 107.99 (16 Oct 2026). Also sold on Ticketmelon in THB (ticket group 'WEEK3: 23 JAN 2027'). Limited tickets. Dice sales end at noon on 23 Jan.
      Line-up, tips & links
      Type
      party
      • All three Saturdays are now in your dates. Sat 23 Jan is the last one. Watch @circolocoibiza on Instagram for the lineup.
      • From Kamala it is about 1 hour by car (44 km). Book your car back before you go.
      • Ask your driver not to stop or wait at the main gate (venue request).
      • Dice says 18+, but Ticketmelon says 20+. Bring your passport.
      • DnB Allstars is on the same Saturday in Chalong, far in the south. Choose one.

      Marco Carola at Café del Mar

      Café del Mar Phuket, Pyramid Stage · Kamala

      Underground 2/5

      Marco Carola, the man behind the Music On residency in Ibiza, plays one of his long sets on the open-air Pyramid Stage. Nicolas Masseyeff supports. Big beach-club crowd, tech house and techno from afternoon into the night. The biggest techno-side name in Phuket in your dates so far.

      tech housetechno
      When
      Wed 13 Jan, 2 PM - 10:30 PM. Clubroom after-party from 11 PM (separate ticket)
      Tickets
      Megatix, 15 Oct 2026: Early Bird 1,900 and 1st Release 2,500 THB (≈27,000 AMD) are sold out. Final Release 3,000 THB (≈32,400 AMD) (entry by 18:00), Anytime Entry 5,000 THB (≈54,000 AMD) with 1 drink. The Clubroom after-party from 23:00 is a separate 1,200 THB (≈13,000 AMD) ticket (sold out).
      Line-up, tips & links
      Lineup
      Marco Carola, Nicolas Masseyeff
      Type
      day party
      • Strictly 20+. Bring ID.
      • Each ticket has an entry time. Late arrival can be refused or cost a 1,000 THB (≈10,800 AMD) fee. Come before 6 PM to avoid queues.
      • The main ticket is the outdoor show only. The after-party in the Clubroom (from 11 PM) needs its own ticket.
      • Ticket tiers sell out fast: buy early.

      Courage Bar (FAKE PALM, SUB and Enthusiast nights)

      COURAGE | КУРАЖ, 16 Bangkok Road, Phuket Old Town · Phuket Town (Old Town)

      Underground 5/5

      Small bar in Phuket Old Town. In the 2025/26 season it hosted some of Phuket's most underground parties: FAKE PALM (techno, breaks), SUB (UK garage, bass, jungle) and WAV.e x Enthusiast (minimal). Parties are not weekly. No dates for 19-25 Jan yet (16 Oct 2026).

      technobreakbeatminimalUK garagedrum and bass
      When
      Irregular parties in high season, mostly on Fridays or Saturdays. Last January: Framework with Sergey Sanchez (Fri 2 Jan 2026), FAKE ORBIT (Sat 17 Jan 2026) and a SUB boat party from Chalong Pier (Tue 27 Jan 2026).
      Tickets
      300-800 THB (≈3,200-8,600 AMD) at 2025/26 parties (RA). FAKE ORBIT (Jan 2026): 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD) (300 THB, ≈3,200 AMD early bird).
      Line-up, tips & links
      Type
      bar
      • Follow Instagram @courage.phuket and @subphuket for January dates. FAKE PALM nights also appear on RA and Megatix.
      • Check the venue on each flyer. SUB also uses other places (The Chill Spot in Karon, Tempo in Chalong, a boat from Chalong Pier).
      • Also watch VESHALKA, an electro and breakbeat crew: it played the bar Вечно Молодой (Vechno Molodoy), 88/15 Kata Road, on 16 Oct 2026 (400 THB, ≈4,300 AMD).
      • Phuket Town is about 40 minutes by car from Kamala. Use Grab or Bolt to get home.

      Retro Mountain Jungle Club

      Retro Mountain Jungle Club, Ban Tai, Koh Phangan · Koh Phangan

      Underground 4/5

      Jungle club on a hill in Ban Tai, Koh Phangan, with two stages and a rain-proof main dance floor. Different crews run the nights: hard techno 'Secret Rave' by Hardtechno KPG, Kovër Crëw techno nights, psytrance, and guests like Nakadia. One of the best places on the islands for dark, hard techno.

      technohard technohousepsytrance
      When
      Usually 1-3 party nights a week; the program changes every week

About 20,000 people, neon paint, fire shows and a long row of bars, each with its own sound system: mostly EDM, plus house, techno, trance and hip-hop. Fun to see once, but the opposite of underground. It falls in your Koh Phangan days.

      When

      Tickets
      Entry 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD), cash only at the beach gates, with a wristband. There is no presale.
      Line-up, tips & links
      Type
      party
      • The full moon is on Fri 22 Jan (7:17 PM Thai time). The official party week is 20-24 Jan.
      • There are no online tickets. The official site says any site that sells them in advance is a scam.
      • Wear closed shoes. There is broken glass on the sand.
      • Leave passport and cards in the room safe. Take cash, a photo of your passport and a waterproof phone pouch.
      • Do not swim at night, and keep away from the fire rope and fire limbo.

      Finding the real underground

      • Small parties are posted only 1 to 3 weeks ahead. Look again in late December and every Monday of your trip.
      • Resident Advisor (ra.co): search Phuket and Koh Phangan.
      • Telegram: the Phangan Party Guide channel (t.me/s/phanganparty) lists each week's parties.
      • Instagram: Shelter Phuket, Courage Bar and its crews, Retro Mountain, Unclave and the Lighthouse Party post line-ups first.
      • Ask DJs and bar staff at Shelter and Courage Bar about after-parties. They spread by word of mouth.
      • Changed since the first research: Bermudos in Rawai has had no parties since about 2023, Niky's Speakeasy could not be confirmed for 2026 (website offline), and OXA plays more tech house than techno.
      Must-see · hidden gems · day trips

      Places to go

      Each place shows how long people usually stay (not the drive), the best time to go and the price. In January the sea on the west coast is calm and clear: the best month for beaches and boat trips.

      Subhrajyoti07 · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      1–2 h

      Big Buddha

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad · Temple · พระพุทธมิ่งมงคลเอกนาคคีรี

      A 45 m white marble Buddha on top of Nakkerd Hill. It closed after a landslide in August 2024 and reopened on 3 March 2026. The terrace has wide views over Kata, Karon and Chalong Bay. It is an active temple, so dress and behave with respect.

      Time
      1–2 h on site
      Best time
      Just after the 9:00 opening: cool air and few people. No sunset here, the gate closes at 18:00.
      Cost
      Free. Donations welcome. Parking and sarongs are free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 9:00-18:00, last entry 17:30 (two 2026 guides; Google Maps still shows 6:00-18:30). Open again since 3 March 2026.
      Getting there
      Hill road from Chaofa West Road (signs from Chalong Circle). Car or scooter: about 35-45 min from Patong, 20-25 min from Kata. Grab and Bolt drive to the top; book the ride back from the car park.
      • Cover shoulders and knees. Free sarongs at the entrance.
      • Sunset is about 18:25 in January, after closing time. Watch it from Nak-Kerd Seaview Cafe on the road down (open to 20:00).
      • The road down is steep with tight bends. Ride slowly on a scooter.
      • Only the statue, main stairs, temple area and terraces are open. Follow the signs and barriers.
      • After heavy rain, check that it is open before you go. Access rules have changed several times since 2024.
      Wikipedia ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      CEphoto, Uwe Aranas · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      1–1.5 h

      Wat Chalong

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad · Temple · วัดฉลอง (วัดไชยธาราราม)

      Phuket's largest and most important Buddhist temple. Climb the 60 m Grand Pagoda: the lower floors have Buddha statues and murals, and the top floor holds a small bone relic of the Buddha. Loud firecrackers are normal: locals light them to give thanks when a wish comes true.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Early morning, about 8:00-9:30, before the heat and the tour buses.
      Cost
      Free. Donations welcome. Free parking.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Temple buildings daily from 7:00 or 8:00 to 17:00 (sources differ). You can walk the grounds outside these hours.
      Getting there
      On Chaofa West Road near Chalong Circle. Car or scooter: about 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata. About 15 min by car from the Big Buddha.
      • No shorts or short skirts, no sleeveless tops. Take off shoes and hats before you enter a building.
      • Speak quietly and do not touch the statues.
      • Easy to combine with the Big Buddha and The Distillery Phuket (Chalong Bay Rum) in one trip.
      Wat Chalong website (FAQ) ↗Wikipedia ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Christophe95 · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Phuket Old Town

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Culture · เมืองเก่าภูเก็ต

      The historic center of Phuket Town. Colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era line Thalang, Dibuk, Krabi and Phang Nga roads. Soi Romanee is the prettiest small lane. Come for cafes, street art, Chinese shrines and local food such as Hokkien noodles.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Early morning (8:00-10:00) for empty streets and soft light, or late afternoon. On Sunday, stay for the night market.
      Cost
      Free to walk. Thai Hua Museum: 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD), plus 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) if you want to take photos inside.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public streets, always open. Shop and cafe hours vary.
      Getting there
      Car or Grab: about 25-35 min from Patong (over Patong Hill), 30-40 min from Kata. Parking in the old streets is hard, so Grab is easier.
      • Thai Hua Museum (28 Krabi Rd) explains Phuket's Chinese history, 9:00-17:00. Sources differ on its closed day (Monday, Wednesday, or none on Google), so Sunday is a safe choice.
      • It is hot by 11:00. Walk early, then rest in a cafe.
      • On Sunday 10 or 17 Jan, stay for the Lard Yai walking street market.
      • End the day at Khao Rang Viewpoint for sunset, about 5 min by car.
      Wikipedia ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Christophe95 · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Evening

      Sunday Walking Street Market (Lard Yai)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Market · ถนนคนเดิน หลาดใหญ่

      Every Sunday evening, Thalang Road in the Old Town closes to cars and becomes a 360 m street market. Stalls sell Phuket snacks, handmade crafts and clothes, with music and street shows. It is busy and local, and the old shophouses make a great backdrop.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      Arrive 16:30-17:00. By 19:00-20:00 it is very crowded.
      Cost
      Free entry. Bring small cash notes.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Sundays only, about 16:00-22:00 (Google says to 23:00). On your trip: Sun 10, 17 and 24 Jan 2027. · Only Sun
      Getting there
      Grab or taxi from Patong about 25-30 min (about 300-500 THB, ≈3,200-5,400 AMD, check the app), from Kata 30-40 min. Do not drive: parking near Thalang Road is very hard on Sundays.
      • Try Phuket snacks like o-tao, a-pong and Hokkien noodles.
      • Most stalls take cash only; some take Thai QR payment.
      • Walk the street in one direction and leave at the other end. Turning back in the crowd is slow.
      • Come earlier and see the Old Town in daylight first.

      Google MapsDirections
      edwin.11 · CC BY 2.0
      Must-see
      1–1.5 h

      Promthep Cape

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Viewpoint · แหลมพรหมเทพ

      The southern tip of Phuket and the island's most famous sunset point. Terraces look west over the sea and small islands. Next to the white lighthouse (with a small free museum) is a Brahma shrine surrounded by hundreds of elephant statues. Expect big crowds at sunset.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Sunset, about 18:25 in January. Arrive by 17:30 for parking and a good spot.
      Cost
      Free. Free parking. The small lighthouse museum is free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open 24 hours. The lighthouse museum has shorter hours (about 9:00-17:00 or 18:00, sources differ).
      Getting there
      Southern tip of the island, past Nai Harn. Car or scooter: about 35-45 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata. Traffic is slow right after sunset.
      • Tour buses arrive around 17:00-18:00. Come early, or stay 20 min after sunset when most people leave.
      • The lighthouse museum may close before sunset. Come earlier if you want to see it.
      • A rough path goes down to the tip of the cape. Wear shoes, take water and come back before dark.
      • Less crowded option: Windmill Viewpoint, about 1.3 km north by road.
      • Respect the shrine and do not touch the offerings.

      Google MapsDirections
      shankar s. (Flickr) · CC BY 2.0
      Must-see
      30 min–1 h

      Windmill Viewpoint

      Nai Harn · Viewpoint

      A grassy hilltop next to a large wind turbine, between Nai Harn and Promthep Cape. You look down on small Ya Nui Beach and Koh Man island, with Promthep in the distance. There is a little parking, a shade pavilion and a drinks stall. A calm sunset choice.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon to sunset (about 18:25 in January). Calmer than Promthep Cape.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open hilltop by the road. Google lists it as open 24 hours; a Feb 2026 news report says daily 6:00-19:00.
      Getting there
      On the road from Nai Harn to Promthep Cape: after the lake, go up the hill to a sharp left bend and take the short dirt track. About 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata.
      • Little shade: bring water and a hat in the daytime.
      • The access road is narrow and steep, and the car park is small. A scooter or taxi is easier than a big car.
      • Do Karon Viewpoint, Nai Harn, Windmill and Promthep in one afternoon loop.
      • On clear days you may see paragliders over Ya Nui Beach.

      Google MapsDirections
      shankar s. (Flickr) · CC BY 2.0
      Must-see
      15–30 min

      Karon Viewpoint

      Kata Noi · Viewpoint

      Phuket's classic postcard view: three bays in a row. Kata Noi is below, then Kata with little Koh Pu island, and Karon further north. A quick 15-minute stop with a large car park and small drink stalls, on the way to Nai Harn and Promthep Cape.

      Time
      15–30 min on site
      Best time
      16:00-17:00 for warm light, or early morning for clear air. Midday light is flat.
      Cost
      Free. Free parking.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open 24 hours.
      Getting there
      On the coast road from Kata Noi to Nai Harn. About 5-10 min from Kata, 25-30 min from Patong.
      • The car park fills in the late afternoon in high season. Arrive before 16:00.
      • The dirt road to Black Rock Viewpoint starts a short drive south of here, toward Nai Harn.
      • Drinks and snacks are sold a few steps below the platform.

      Google MapsDirections
      Jacek Lesniowski · CC BY-SA 3.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Kata Beach

      Kata (Kata Yai) · Beach · หาดกะตะ

      A 1.5 km bay of soft sand with Koh Pu island in front. From December to April the sea is usually calm and clear, good for swimming. It is more relaxed than Patong, with shade trees, beach restaurants and massages. The south end is the liveliest in the evening.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning for a calm swim. Sunset (about 18:25) with Koh Pu island in front.
      Cost
      Free. Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent (price varies). Beach massage from about 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      In Kata: walk. From Patong about 20-30 min by car, scooter or Grab.
      • Always respect red flags. Rip currents can still happen.
      • Sunbeds use only a small part of the beach. Bring a towel if you do not want to rent.
      • For sunset drinks, walk to the south end, where Ska Bar sits on the rocks.
      Wikipedia ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Tuderna · CC BY 3.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Kata Noi Beach

      Kata Noi · Beach · หาดกะตะน้อย

      A small, quieter bay just south of Kata, with soft white sand and clear water. In the dry season the sea is calm and good for swimming, and lifeguards work in the daytime. Most of the beachfront is taken by one big resort, Katathani, so there are few shops or bars.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Before 10:00: easier parking and shade at both ends.
      Cost
      Free. No public sunbed rental: sunbeds and umbrellas are only for guests of Katathani and The Shore.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      About 5 min by car or 15-20 min on foot (hilly road) from Kata. 25-30 min from Patong. Small car park at the south end near Katathani, plus a few roadside spots.
      • Bring a towel or mat and your own shade.
      • The middle of the beach has no shade after mid-morning. Sit near the trees at either end.
      • Karon Viewpoint is 5 min up the hill.

      Google MapsDirections
      ADwarf · Public domain
      Must-see
      Half day

      Nai Harn Beach

      Nai Harn · Beach · หาดในหาน

      A wide, natural bay in the far south of the island. The land behind the sand is protected, so there are no buildings, only tall casuarina trees. The water is clear blue in high season. Simple Thai restaurants are across the small road, and a temple and lake are behind the beach.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning or late afternoon. December and January can be busy.
      Cost
      Free. Beach massage about 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) per hour.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      Car or scooter: about 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata.
      • A stream from the lake crosses the south end of the beach. Your feet will get wet.
      • Good base for sunset: Windmill Viewpoint and Promthep Cape are each 5-10 min away by car.
      • For a sunset drink, try Reflections Rooftop Bar at The Nai Harn hotel (opens 17:00).

      Google MapsDirections
      Joachim Lutz · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Freedom Beach

      Patong & Kalim · Beach

      A 300 m cove of soft white sand and clear water just south of Patong. You arrive by longtail boat or by a steep jungle trail, so it is much calmer than the big beaches. There is some snorkeling at both ends. Barefoot Bistro at the south end serves food and drinks.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning on a calm day. Boats run mainly from December to May.
      Cost
      Longtail from Patong: about 1,000-1,500 THB (≈10,800-16,200 AMD) return per boat. Walk-in: free to 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) per person, depending on the path (sources differ). Scooter parking may cost about 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daytime only. Boat access is mainly December-May.
      Getting there
      Longtail boat from the south end of Patong Beach (near Amari), about 10 min. Or drive to The Lek Sand Beach Bar on the Patong-Karon hill road and hike down 15-25 min. The trailhead is about 15 min from Patong, 25 min from Kata.
      • Agree the boat price and pickup time before you leave Patong.
      • There is no pier: you step off the boat into the water. Use a dry bag.
      • The hike back up is hard. Sometimes a 4x4 ride up costs about 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) per person.
      • Toilets and showers may be closed. Bring water, snorkel gear and real shoes for the trail.

      Google MapsDirections
      Arnaud-Victor Monteux · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Patong Beach

      Patong & Kalim · Beach · หาดป่าตอง

      Phuket's busiest and most famous beach: 3 km of sand in front of the main party town. Expect jet skis, parasailing, vendors and crowds in the center. The north end is quieter, with softer sand and cleaner water. The south end has longtail boats to Freedom Beach.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning for a calmer swim; sunset from the sand. The north end is quieter all day.
      Cost
      Free. Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      In Patong: walk. From Kata about 20-30 min by car, scooter or Grab.
      • Smoking is banned on Patong Beach outside marked smoking areas. The fine can be up to 100,000 THB (≈1,080,000 AMD).
      • Some jet ski renters claim damage after the ride. Take photos of the jet ski before you start, or skip it.
      • For a quieter swim, go to the north end.
      • Beach clubs: Kudo and Barra Cuda in the center, Fuga at the north end.
      TAT news: smoking ban on Thai beaches ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Ben Reeves from Phuket, Thailand · CC BY 2.0
      Must-see
      Evening

      Bangla Road

      Patong & Kalim · Nightlife · ถนนบางลา

      Patong's famous 400 m party street. Neon beer bars, go-go bars, live music bars and big clubs like Illuzion fill it every night. Loud, chaotic and worth seeing once. The music is mostly commercial EDM, hip-hop and cover bands, not underground techno.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      19:00-21:00 to look around; after 22:00 for the full party.
      Cost
      Free to walk. Beer about 100-180 THB (≈1,100-1,900 AMD), cocktails 200-350 THB (≈2,200-3,800 AMD). Club entry varies.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Pedestrian street every night from about 18:00. Licensed venues open to 4:00; small bars often close about 2:00.
      Getting there
      In Patong: walk. From Kata about 20-30 min by Grab or taxi.
      • Ignore touts with show cards. They do not work for the bars.
      • Check menu prices before you order.
      • Bangla Street Food stays open late if you are hungry after midnight.
      • Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket in the crowd.

      Google MapsDirections
      Christophe95 · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      30 min–2 h

      Khao Rang Viewpoint

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Viewpoint · จุดชมวิวเขารัง

      A green hill right above Phuket Town. A viewing deck looks over the city, Chalong Bay and Cape Panwa. Hilltop restaurants such as Tunk Ka Cafe serve Thai food with the same view. A good end to an Old Town day, especially at sunset.

      Time
      30 min–2 h on site
      Best time
      Sunset (about 18:25 in January) and the 20 min after, when the town lights come on.
      Cost
      Free. Tunk Ka Cafe mains about 80-180 THB (≈860-1,900 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Viewing deck: free, listed as open 24 hours. Tunk Ka Cafe: daily about 11:00-22:00.
      Getting there
      A few minutes uphill from Phuket Old Town. About 25-35 min from Patong, 30-40 min from Kata.
      • Book a rail-side table at Tunk Ka Cafe by phone (081 892 6315) and arrive about 18:00.
      • Monkeys live near the top. Do not feed them and keep food in closed bags.
      • Phuket Old Town is about 5 min away by car.

      Google MapsDirections
      © Naka Night Market Phuket · official site
      Must-see
      Evening

      Naka Weekend Market

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Market

      Phuket's biggest weekend night market, on the south edge of Phuket Town. Hundreds of stalls sell cheap clothes, souvenirs and gadgets, plus a large street-food area. There is live music on the stage in the evening. Busy, hot and very local.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      Arrive 16:30-17:30, before the big evening crowd and the parking jam.
      Cost
      Free entry.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Saturday and Sunday 16:00-22:00 (Google, Phuket 101 and the official site footer; the official home page says 23:00). On your trip: Sat 9, Sun 10, Sat 16, Sun 17, Sat 23 and Sun 24 Jan 2027. On weekdays only the street-food zone is open. · Only Sat, Sun
      Getting there
      South edge of Phuket Town, near Central Phuket. About 20-30 min from Patong, 25-35 min from Kata. The car park at the back jams at night; roadside parking is often easier.
      • Bargain for clothes and souvenirs, but not for food.
      • Bring small cash notes.
      • Eat early, around 17:00, then shop when it cools down.
      • Local guitarist Nene Royal often plays the new stage at about 19:00 on market nights.
      Official site ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      JULIANISME · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Evening

      Chillva Market

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Market

      A trendy night market in Phuket Town, popular with young Thais. Local fashion stalls and street food sit between bars built from stacked shipping containers, some with upstairs seats. A stage has live music. Smaller and more creative than Naka.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      18:00-19:00 for the best stalls and the start of live music. Wednesday-Thursday calmer, Friday-Saturday livelier.
      Cost
      Free entry.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Monday to Saturday, 17:00-23:00. Closed Sunday (10, 17 and 24 Jan on your trip). Tuesday adds a second-hand clothes market (Tue 12 and Tue 19 Jan). · Only Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat
      Getting there
      141/2 Yaowarat Road, north side of Phuket Town. About 20-30 min from Patong, 30-40 min from Kata. Parking on site, busy on weekend evenings.
      • Bring cash in small notes. Do not count on paying by phone.
      • On Fridays, get to the container bars early for an upstairs seat.
      • The quieter Retro Area at the back is good for a drink.

      Google MapsDirections
      Andy Mitchell from Glasgow, UK · CC BY-SA 2.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Nai Yang Beach (Sirinat National Park)

      Nai Yang · Beach · หาดในยาง

      A quiet, shady bay inside Sirinat National Park, next to the airport. Small seafood restaurants and bars sit under the trees, and the sea is calm in high season. About 2.5 km north, at Mai Khao Beach, planes land low over the sand in the dry season.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Late afternoon: shade, plane landings and sunset (about 18:25-18:30). On your flight day, Tue 26 Jan, come in the late morning and leave by about 14:45.
      Cost
      Village part of the beach: free. Sirinat National Park fee for foreigners: 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) adult, 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) child, charged in the park area.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Beach always open. Sirinat National Park office: 8:00-16:30.
      Getting there
      5-10 min from Phuket Airport. About 45-60 min from Patong, 60-75 min from Kata.
      • Plane spotting: the south end of Mai Khao Beach, best from late morning to about 14:00 (see its card).
      • Stay out of the airport safety zone under the approach path. No drones, lasers or flash: penalties are heavy.
      • Flight day, Tue 26 Jan: the terminal is only 5-10 minutes by car. Leave the beach by about 14:45 to be there by 15:20.
      • Lunch on the sand: Sea Almond (Google 4.4, 855 reviews), Phen's (4.3, 1,260) and The Good View. For a bigger Southern Thai meal, Natural Restaurant is 2.4 km inland (see its card).
      • With luggage on the last day, leave your bags at your hotel or at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht, ≈1,600 AMD per bag) before you go to the beach.

      Google MapsDirections
      Jeff Gunn · CC BY 2.0
      Must-see
      1.5–2.5 h

      Bang Pae Waterfall (Khao Phra Thaeo)

      Thalang · Waterfall · น้ำตกบางแป

      The largest waterfall on Phuket, inside the Khao Phra Thaeo rainforest reserve. A 10-15 minute jungle path follows the stream to the falls and rock pools. In January the flow is getting low, so think forest walk, not big waterfall. The Gibbon Rehabilitation Project is at the entrance.

      Time
      1.5–2.5 h on site
      Best time
      Weekday morning, before 10:00. In January the water is lower than in the rainy season.
      Cost
      Park fee for foreigners: 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) adult, 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) child in most sources. Phuket 101's FAQ and some visitor reviews say 400/200 THB (≈4,300/2,200 AMD), so carry 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD) per adult in cash. The same-day ticket is also valid at Ton Sai Waterfall.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily, daytime. Google and Thai Holiday Guide say 9:00-16:00; other sources say 8:00-17:00 or 8:00-18:00. Arrive before 15:00.
      Getting there
      Off Route 4027 on the east side of the island. About 40-50 min from Patong, 50-60 min from Kata. About 10 min from the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary office.
      • Gibbon project: visits only in booked sessions (1 hour at 10:30, 12:30 or 14:00, or 2.5 hours from 9:30). On days with no bookings it is closed. Book online first.
      • Wear shoes with grip. The rocks are slippery; do not jump from them.
      • Alcohol is not allowed in the park.
      • Ton Sai Waterfall (same ticket) is very small in the dry season.
      Gibbon Rehabilitation Project booking ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © Phuket Elephant Sanctuary · official site
      Must-see
      Half day

      Phuket Elephant Sanctuary

      Thalang · Activity

      An ethical sanctuary for rescued and retired elephants. There is no riding, no bathing and, since 1 April 2026, no feeding. You watch the elephants roam, forage and bathe freely from forest trails and a long canopy walkway. Lunch is a vegetarian Thai buffet.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning program (about 9:30-13:00) is cooler. Book several days ahead in high season.
      Cost
      Half day: 3,000 THB (≈32,400 AMD) per adult (age 13+). Child prices on the booking page. Shared hotel transfer can be added. Shorter Canopy Walkway Tour (1.5 hours) from 1,900 THB (≈20,500 AMD). Full day from 7,000 THB (≈75,600 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Every day except 13 April. Half-day programs: morning about 9:30-13:00, afternoon about 13:30-17:00. Booking required, no walk-ins.
      Getting there
      Meet at the sanctuary office in Paklok (this pin), or book the shared hotel pickup. Self-drive about 40-50 min from Patong, 45-60 min from Kata.
      • Book online first. There is no public access to the sanctuary; every visit starts at the office.
      • Wear clothes that can get dirty. Rubber boots, raincoats and mosquito spray are provided.
      • The visit includes the elephant hospital, Phuket's first.
      • Combine with Bang Pae Waterfall, about 10 min away.
      • Google's pin for the sanctuary is about 650 m from the meeting office. Use 'Directions to the office'.
      Official half-day program ↗

      Google MapsDirections to the office
      © The Distillery Phuket (Chalong Bay Rum) · official site
      Must-see
      1–2.5 h

      Chalong Bay Rum Distillery (The Distillery Phuket)

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad · Activity

      The Distillery Phuket, home of Chalong Bay Rum, was started in 2012 by two French expats. They make rum from fresh Thai sugarcane juice, plus Saneha gin and Lanna vodka. The 1-hour tour ends with a tasting and a mojito. The bar and restaurant in the sugarcane garden are good for dinner.

      Time
      1–2.5 h on site
      Best time
      Take the 17:00 tour, then stay for dinner and cocktails in the garden.
      Cost
      Distillery tour 590 THB (≈6,400 AMD) (with a mojito and a tasting of 9 flavours). Cocktail workshops 990-1,490 THB (≈10,700-16,100 AMD). Booking required.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Bar and restaurant daily 11:00-23:00 (official site; Google says until 22:00). Tours daily at 13:00, 15:00, 17:00 and 19:00 (1 hour).
      Getting there
      14/2 Moo 2, Soi Palai 2, Chalong. About 30-40 min from Patong, 15-20 min from Kata.
      • Book on the official site before you go.
      • Photos are not allowed inside the distillery.
      • After the tasting, take Grab instead of riding a scooter.
      • Cocktail workshops start at 12:00 (vodka), 14:00 (rum) and 16:00 (gin).
      Official distillery visit page ↗Official cocktail workshop page ↗Official bar and restaurant page ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Айрат Хайруллин · CC BY 3.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Karon Beach

      Karon · Beach · หาดกะรน

      A wide 3 km beach of soft, pale sand between Patong and Kata. Most hotels are across the beach road, so the sand rarely feels crowded. From December to April the sea is usually calm for swimming. The dry sand squeaks under your feet. Good for long walks at sunset.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning for calm water and space. Late afternoon for a long walk and sunset (about 18:25).
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      In Karon you walk to the sand. From Patong about 15 min over the hill road, from Kamala about 30-40 min, by car, scooter or Grab. Kata is next door to the south.
      • Always check the flags. Rip currents are mainly a May-October problem, but they can still happen.
      • The north end is the quietest part. After heavy rain, dark water from the canal near Nong Harn lake can run across the sand there. Swim away from it.
      • The south end, near Kata, has TANN Beach Club (11:00-23:00) with a fire show every night at about 19:00.
      • Karon Temple Market runs Tuesday and Friday, 16:00-22:00, at Wat Karon, about 10 minutes on foot from the middle of the beach.
      • Jet skis and parasailing work off the sand in high season. Swim away from them.

      Google MapsDirections
      Ralf Schmidt · CC BY-SA 3.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Kamala Beach

      Kamala · Beach · หาดกมลา

      About 2 km of soft, pale sand with shade trees. The quiet town behind it grew from a Muslim fishing village. It is the base suggested in this guide. In the high season the sea is shallow, calm and clear, one of the easiest swims on the island. Small Thai restaurants and bamboo bars sit on the sand, good for sunset.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning swim at the north or central part. Sunset (about 18:25) at a bar on the sand.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      In Kamala you walk to the sand. From Patong about 15 min over the hill road, from the airport about 35-45 min, by car or Grab.
      • Swim at the north or central part. At the south end, streams bring brown water and fishing boats park.
      • For sunset, sit at one of the small bamboo bars in the middle of the beach, or at Pine Beach Bar (8:00-23:00) on the sand below the InterContinental at the north end.
      • Smile Bar on the beach (13:00-22:00) is a classic Kamala meal: grilled chicken, sticky rice and som tam.
      • Café del Mar is at the north end of the beach. See Events for its January shows.
      • Rip currents are a June-November problem. In January the sea is usually calm, but check the flags.

      Google MapsDirections
      Maleewan1wanpen2thai · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Must-see
      Half day

      Surin Beach

      Surin & Pansea · Beach · หาดสุรินทร์

      An 800 m bay of soft, pale sand with casuarina trees for shade, 5-10 minutes north of Kamala. Between 2023 and May 2025 the bars, sunbeds and beach massage were removed from the sand, so it looks natural again. From December to April the water is often clear and calm: some of the best swimming on the island.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning, for the clearest water and shade under the trees. Or late afternoon for sunset (about 18:25).
      Cost
      Free. In early 2026 there were no sunbeds or umbrellas for rent.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Always open.
      Getting there
      About 5-10 min north of Kamala by car, scooter or Grab. About 20 min from Patong.
      • Bring a towel or mat. In early 2026 visitors found no sunbeds or umbrellas to rent. Food and drinks are sold at stalls by the car park and in cafes across the road.
      • Eat at Tukta Food & Drink, on the rocks at the south end (10:30-21:00). The stairs to the upper floors are hidden, but the view is worth it.
      • From the south end, walk 15-20 min over the rocks (easier at mid to low tide), or take the 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) boat, to Laem Singh Beach. The boat may not run in bad weather.
      • In the low season (May-October) the sea can be rough. In January it is usually calm, but some visitors report deep water and currents a few metres out. Check the flags.

      Google MapsDirections
      The Cosmonaut · CC BY-SA 2.5 ca
      Must-see
      1–2 h

      Plane spotting at Mai Khao Beach

      Mai Khao · Activity · จุดชมวิวเครื่องบิน หาดไม้ขาว

      At the south end of Mai Khao Beach, planes pass very low over your head just before they land at Phuket Airport. In the high season the wind comes from the east, so most planes come in over the sea and the sand. It is loud, a little crazy and free. Drink and food stalls wait at the car park and the runway end.

      Time
      1–2 h on site
      Best time
      Late morning to about 14:00, when more planes land. Low tide gives a wider beach for photos. From December to June most planes land over the sea. On your flight day, Tue 26 Jan, come about 11:00-13:30.
      Cost
      Free. Motorbike ride from the car park to the runway end: 20 THB (≈220 AMD). If you come in through Sirinat National Park from the Nai Yang side, the park fee can apply (200 THB, ≈2,200 AMD per foreign adult in 2026).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open beach. Planes land all day.
      Getting there
      Drive north past the airport and follow the signs with a plane picture to the car park by the beach. Walk about 500 m south on the sand to the end of the runway, or take a 20 THB (≈220 AMD) motorbike ride. About 20 min from the terminal (the road goes around the runway), 40-50 min from Kamala, about 60 min from Patong.
      • Open the FlightRadar24 app to see when the next plane lands. Planes that come in from the west, over the sea, pass over the beach.
      • Watch from the side. Standing in the landing path is not allowed, and jet blast from planes waiting to take off throws sand hard.
      • If the wind is from the west, planes land from the other side and only take-offs pass over the beach. In January the wind is usually from the east.
      • Do not fly a drone. The beach is next to the runway, in the airport no-fly zone.
      • Bring a cap and water. There is no shade on the sand.
      • Good last stop on Tue 26 Jan: watch until about 13:30-14:00, walk back to the car park, then drive about 20 minutes around the runway to the terminal (be there by 15:20).
      • With luggage on the last day, come with a driver who waits for you, or first leave your bags at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht, ≈1,600 AMD per bag).

      Google MapsDirections
      Karelj · CC BY 4.0
      Must-see
      Evening

      Bangla Boxing Stadium (Muay Thai fight night)

      Patong & Kalim · Activity · สนามมวยบางลา

      Patong's Muay Thai stadium, open since 2004, with fights every night. A card has about 8 bouts, from teenagers up to the main fights, with live traditional music and the Wai Kru dance before each bout. An English commentator explains the action. It is for tourists and not cheap, but a fun first look at Thai boxing.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      Arrive by about 20:45 to get your T-shirt and seat before the first bout at 21:00. The strongest fights are at the end of the card.
      Cost
      Stadium seat 1,600 THB (≈17,300 AMD), Ringside 2,000 THB (≈21,600 AMD), the same online or at the gate (official site, Oct 2026). A free T-shirt is included. Drinks are extra.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Every night. Doors 20:00, first bout 21:00, ends about midnight.
      Getting there
      155/16 Phang Muang Sai Kor Road, Patong, behind Jungceylon mall and opposite Banzaan Fresh Market. About 5-10 min on foot from Bangla Road. From Kamala about 15-25 min by car or Grab.
      • Book online or pay at the gate: the price is the same. Seats fill faster from November to April, so book a day or two ahead.
      • Stadium seats are raised, so you see the whole ring. At Ringside you look up through the ropes.
      • The first bouts are young teenagers. The best fighters come at the end.
      • Wednesday and Saturday cards also have MMA bouts.
      • Shelter, the techno room at Illuzion, is about 10 minutes away on foot, so you can go on after the last fight.
      Official site ↗Tickets and fight dates (official) ↗

      Roma Neus · CC BY 3.0Same headland, from the air
      Hidden gem
      1–1.5 h

      Black Rock Viewpoint (Pa Hin Dam)

      Nai Harn · Viewpoint · ผาหินดำ

      One of the best views in south Phuket. From a rocky hilltop about 290 m high you see Nai Harn Bay, Ao Sane, Koh Man and Promthep Cape. Getting there takes effort: a bumpy dirt road, then a short, steep forest path. Few people, no shops, no railings.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Early morning or late afternoon. Midday is very hot. Start down before dark (sunset about 18:25).
      Cost
      Free. No source reports a fee for the viewpoint.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open hillside, no gate.
      Getting there
      From Karon Viewpoint drive toward Nai Harn and take the second road on the right (sign 'Nui Beach'). After about 1 km of dirt road, keep left at the fork (Thai sign ผาหินดำ). About 500 m later, park at the rock painted 'PA HIN DUM' and walk up about 10 min. About 15-25 min from Kata, 40-50 min from Patong.
      • Wear sneakers, not flip-flops. The path is steep and loose in places.
      • A scooter handles the dirt road better than a car. Skip it after heavy rain.
      • There are no railings at the top. Stay away from the cliff edge.
      • Bring water; there is nothing to buy at the top.
      • There are no lights on the trail. Start down before it gets dark.

      Google MapsDirections
      Anton Zelenov · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Hidden gem
      Half day

      Banana Beach

      Layan · Beach · หาดบานาน่า

      Small cove with soft sand, clear water and rocks for snorkelling at both ends. Late in 2025 the old jungle path closed. Now you park at a new car park at the north end, next to a new beach club with music. The old family restaurant further south is still open.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Weekday morning, before 10:00. The sea is calm from November to April.
      Cost
      Beach free. Parking 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD). Toilet and shower 20 THB (≈220 AMD). Sunbeds extra.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach, best in daylight.
      Getting there
      Car or scooter, on the coast road between Layan and Nai Thon. The car park is at the north end of the beach, between Trisara resort and Andaman White Beach Resort. Coming from Bang Tao, pass Trisara and turn left. Coming from Nai Thon, pass Andaman White Beach Resort and turn right. From the car park you are on the sand in one minute.
      • Arrive before 10:00. By midday the sunbeds near the beach club are full.
      • Walk south to the old Banana Beach Restaurant. Simple Thai food and seafood, fair prices, no loud music.
      • Bring your own snorkel mask. The beach club rents gear, but it costs more.
      • Avoid weekends and Thai holidays. The beach is small and fills fast.
      • In Google Maps the new beach club is 'Banana Beach Club by Sollis 2.0' (10:00-20:00).

      Google MapsDirections
      Roma Neus · CC BY 3.0
      Hidden gem
      Half day

      Laem Singh Beach

      Surin & Pansea · Beach · หาดแหลมสิงห์

      A 300 m cove with golden sand, big granite boulders and clear water, between Surin and Kamala. The road access closed in 2017, so you come by a short boat ride or a rocky walk. Because of this it feels almost empty, even in high season. One small Thai restaurant on the rocks. No sunbeds, shops or toilets.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Morning, when the boulders give shade. Walk in at mid or low tide.
      Cost
      Free if you walk. Boat 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) per person, and the ride back is included (keep the numbered card). About 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD) to charter the boat.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daylight. The boat runs only in good weather.
      Getting there
      Go to the far south end of Surin Beach. Walk past Tukta Food & Drink (Tukta Restaurant) to the rocks. The path takes 15-20 minutes, with boulders at the start. Or take the small boat from the same spot. No road access since 2017.
      • Wear trainers or sport sandals. The first rocks are slippery.
      • At high tide take the boat. Waves wash over the low part of the path.
      • Bring cash. The restaurant takes cash only and there is no ATM nearby.
      • The best snorkelling is at the south rocks, toward Kamala. Take your rubbish back with you.

      Google MapsDirections
      Christophe95 · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Hidden gem
      2–3 h

      Ya Nui Beach

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Beach · หาดยะนุ้ย

      Tiny cove split in two by a small rocky hill, with the island Koh Man in front. Clear water and rocks make it one of the easiest snorkel spots in the south. You can rent kayaks and paddle boards. Two simple Thai restaurants under the trees. It is small, so it can be busy at peak times.

      Time
      2–3 h on site
      Best time
      Morning, for calm water and snorkelling. Weekdays are quieter.
      Cost
      Free. Snorkel set 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD), kayak 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) per hour, stand-up paddle board 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) per hour (Phuket 101, May 2026).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach. Rentals and the two restaurants work in the daytime.
      Getting there
      On the coast road between Nai Harn and Promthep Cape, at the lowest curve of the road. Park along the road or on the small side road. About 22 km from Patong.
      • In calm weather, paddle a kayak out toward Koh Man island.
      • Parking is limited. Come early or use a scooter.
      • Combine with Summore Day cafe and sunset at Promthep Cape, both a few minutes up the road.

      Google MapsDirections
      Roma Neus · CC BY 3.0
      Hidden gem
      2–4 h

      Tri Trang Beach

      Patong & Kalim · Beach · หาดไตรตรัง

      Quiet bay only a few kilometres south of Patong, but it feels far away. Palm trees, one row of beach chairs and the Rosewood resort behind. At low tide rocks and coral show, so swim at high tide. Good snorkelling near the rocks. Small cafes with big views sit on the hill road to Paradise Beach.

      Time
      2–4 h on site
      Best time
      Morning, and at high tide for swimming. No sunset here, the sun goes down behind the cape.
      Cost
      Free. Sunbeds at The HideOut are free with a food or drink order.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach, daylight.
      Getting there
      From Patong drive south over the high bridge toward Amari Phuket and turn left just before the hotel. After Phuket Marriott Merlin Beach on the left, the main beach entrance is about 500 m further on the right. Roads are steep and winding.
      • Wear water shoes. The seabed is rocky.
      • Blue Harbour Coffee and Sunshine View Restaurant on the hill road have wide views over the bay.
      • The HideOut Area restaurant is the only place where you eat on the sand.

      Google MapsDirections

      Hidden gem
      Half day

      Ao Yon Beach

      Cape Panwa · Beach · หาดอ่าวยน

      Long, quiet bay on the east side of the island, near Cape Panwa. Tall palm trees, a few small beach restaurants and bars, and mostly locals and long-time residents. It still feels like old Phuket. Good for a slow walk, lunch and a swim far from the west-coast crowds.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Weekdays. Some weekends locals hold dragon boat or sailing races here.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach. Flamingo Beach Club 10:00-22:00, The Cove 07:30-23:00, Akoya Star Lounge 17:00-23:00 (Google, Oct 2026).
      Getting there
      On Cape Panwa, south-east of Phuket Town. Take Sakdidej Road toward Cape Panwa. Before Panwa Beach, turn right onto Ao Yon-Khao Khad Road; the beach is below this road. The way down is easy to miss, so look for small restaurant signs. Park on the road and walk down. You need a car or scooter.
      • Akoya Star Lounge, the rooftop bar at V Villas, opens 17:00-23:00 and is busy. Book ahead.
      • The Cove, a small resort restaurant and bar in the second bay at the east end, sits right by the water.
      • Combine with the Khao Khad viewpoint tower, about 3 km up the same road.

      Google MapsDirections
      Maleewan1wanpen2thai · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Hidden gem
      2–4 h

      Layan Beach

      Layan · Beach · หาดลายัน

      Quiet north end of Bang Tao Bay. The sand runs north to a small river mouth, with a big island offshore. Locals and expats come for a long lunch, a swim and a massage. The small beach restaurants were removed. Tan Restaurant and Massage, where the road meets the beach, is the last one left.

      Time
      2–4 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon to sunset. Weekdays are the quietest.
      Cost
      Free. Thai massage at Tan Restaurant (old price list: about 400 THB, ≈4,300 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach.
      Getting there
      In Bang Tao, follow the signs to Banyan Tree. Pass the Banyan Tree gates, turn right at the T-junction and drive a few kilometres to the end of the road. Street parking only; the road is narrow.
      • Bring water and snacks. Food choice on the sand is very small now.
      • The beach faces west, so the sunset over the sea and the island is good.
      • For a drink with a view, Beach House and Rooftop by Anantara at Anantara Layan is a short drive north.

      Google MapsDirections
      Roma Neus · CC BY 3.0
      Hidden gem
      2–3 h

      Sai Kaew Beach

      Mai Khao · Beach · หาดทรายแก้ว

      Long, empty white-sand beach at the far north tip of Phuket, just before the Sarasin Bridge. Shallow water, small waves in the dry season and kilometres of sand to walk. Only one bamboo restaurant is left on the sand, serving Thai seafood. Leatherback turtles sometimes nest on this coast from November to February.

      Time
      2–3 h on site
      Best time
      Weekday. Late morning for lunch, or late afternoon for sunset with the Sarasin Bridge.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach. Sai Kaew Beach Restaurant: daily 9:00-21:00 (Google).
      Getting there
      Far north of the island. From the airport, drive north on Highway 402 toward Sarasin Bridge, about 15 minutes. The beach is on the left before the bridge. In Google Maps, 'Sai Kaew Beach Restaurant' marks the way in. You need a car or scooter.
      • Order lunch around 11:30, walk the beach, and eat when you come back.
      • Bring water and a towel. There are no shops, and little shade outside the restaurant area.
      • Easy stop on the way to Natai and Phang Nga, just over the bridge.
      • Ta Tuay, a Michelin-listed local restaurant near the bridge (11:30-21:00), needs a booking.

      Google MapsDirections
      นายอชิระ · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Hidden gem
      2–3 h

      Laem Krating Viewpoint

      Kata Noi · Viewpoint · แหลมกระทิง

      Wild grassy cape on the south-west coast, west of Nai Harn Beach. After a rough 30-minute walk you get open sea views, big waves on the rocks and Promthep Cape in the distance. It stays quiet. There are no fences, signs or facilities, so it is only for fit walkers in dry weather.

      Time
      2–3 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon. Sunset is about 18:25 in January and it is dark by about 18:50. Start about 1.5 hours before sunset.
      Cost
      Free. No facilities.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Open nature area, no gate. Daylight only.
      Getting there
      From Nai Harn Beach take the road past Ao Sane toward Baan Krating Phuket resort. After the resort an unmarked path goes over rock, grass and scrub to the cape, about 30-35 minutes on foot.
      • Wear real shoes with grip. Flip-flops do not work here.
      • Do not go alone, in rain or after dark. The cliff edges have no fence.
      • Bring water and a torch for the way back.
      • Ao Sane beach on the route: Phuket 101 (Mar 2026) says it is closed for construction. Check on the spot before you plan a swim.
      • A guided hike from COMO Point Yamu costs from 3,300 THB (≈35,600 AMD) per adult. Book 24 hours ahead.
      COMO guided hike (Black Rock and Laem Krating) ↗

      Hidden gem
      30 min–1 h

      Khao Khad Viewpoint Tower

      Cape Panwa · Viewpoint · หอชมวิวเขาขาด

      Small viewing tower on Khao Khad hill, on the road to Cape Panwa. From the top you get a 360-degree view: Chalong Bay, Phuket Town, Cape Panwa and many small islands. It is calmer than the big west-coast viewpoints. Free, with a car park, toilets and a few stalls at the bottom.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon for clear light, or a clear early morning. Avoid midday heat.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily, about 06:00-21:00 (Thai Holiday Guide, Jul 2026). Another guide says until 19:00. Google lists no hours.
      Getting there
      On the hill road from Phuket Town to Cape Panwa (Sakdidet Road, Wichit), about 15-20 minutes from Phuket Town by car or scooter. No public transport. Park at the base, then walk up about 200 steps (10-15 minutes) to the tower.
      • There is no shade on the stairs. Bring water and a hat.
      • Show the Thai name จุดชมวิวเขาขาด (or หอชมวิวเขาขาด) to drivers.
      • Combine with Ao Yon Beach and a seafood dinner in the Panwa area.

      Google MapsDirections
      © Bang Rong Connect · official site
      Hidden gem
      1.5–3 h

      Bang Rong Pier and Mangrove Walk

      Ao Po & Cape Yamu · Nature · บ้านบางโรง

      Small Muslim fishing village on the quiet north-east coast, with the pier for boats to Koh Yao. A wooden boardwalk goes through the mangroves to a floating community restaurant with fresh seafood and views of the boats. Kayaks can be rented to paddle into the mangrove channels; ask ahead.

      Time
      1.5–3 h on site
      Best time
      Lunch time on a weekday. Check the tide: the last part of the walkway to the floating restaurant is steep at low tide.
      Cost
      Free to walk. Food is paid. Community half-day tour from 2,800 THB (≈30,200 AMD) per person (at least 2 people, book 2-3 days ahead, hotel transfer not included).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Community seafood restaurant daily 10:30-18:30 (Google listing). Community tourism office about 08:00-18:00.
      Getting there
      North-east coast. Coming north on the Pa Khlok road, turn right at the mosque about 1 km north of the Bang Pae Waterfall entrance, and drive to the pier. About 35 km from Patong. Car or scooter. Parking is free if you only eat or look around.
      • No alcohol here. This is a Muslim community, so dress modestly.
      • The community runs half-day tours (pineapple farm, rubber tapping, coconut and cooking). Book at bangrongconnect.com 2-3 days ahead.
      • Kayak: old reports say about 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) per hour at the restaurant. A 2026 guide says to arrange kayaks and boats in advance.
      • Boats to Koh Yao Noi and Koh Yao Yai leave from this pier.
      Bang Rong community tourism (official) ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © Gibbon Rehabilitation Project · official site
      Hidden gem
      1.5–3 h

      Gibbon Rehabilitation Project

      Thalang · Nature · โครงการคืนชะนีสู่ป่า

      Small charity that rescues gibbons from the tourist trade and returns them to the forest. In a one-hour session a guide explains the work at the edge of Phuket's last rainforest. Only 36 visitors a day are allowed, to keep contact with the gibbons low. A calm, honest nature stop.

      Time
      1.5–3 h on site
      Best time
      Morning session (10:30), when the forest is cooler.
      Cost
      1,100 THB (≈11,900 AMD) adult when booked online (1,200 THB, ≈13,000 AMD walk-in), child 5-14 650 THB (≈7,000 AMD), under 5 free. Plus national park fee 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD) adult, 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) child, cash only at the gate.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Visits only in a learning session: 1 hour at 10:30, 12:30 or 14:00, or 2.5 hours 09:30-12:00 (booked on Airbnb). On days with no bookings there are no staff and the project is closed.
      Getting there
      At the Bang Pae Waterfall entrance of Khao Phra Thaeo National Park, north-east Phuket, about 20 km from Phuket Town. No hotel pickup: come by car, scooter or taxi.
      • Book online at least 4 hours before the session. Walk-ins may find it full, or closed if nobody booked.
      • Bang Pae Waterfall is a short walk away. In January it has less water than in the rainy season (June-November).
      • A jungle trail links Ton Sai and Bang Pae waterfalls. Do not walk it alone; ask the park rangers about a guide.
      • Peang Prai, a Thai restaurant at the park entrance listed in the Michelin Guide, is good for lunch.
      Book a visit (official) ↗1-hour session tickets ↗

      Maxence (Flickr) · CC BY 2.0Monkeys by the island road
      Hidden gem
      1.5–2.5 h

      Koh Sirey: Hilltop Temple and Sea Gypsy Village

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Temple · เกาะสิเหร่

      Small island joined to Phuket Town by a short bridge. On the hilltop, Wat Ban Koh Sirey has a long golden reclining Buddha and a wide view over Phuket Town. Below is Laem Tukkae, a working village of the Urak Lawoi sea people. It is quiet compared with the beach areas. Monkeys live near the bridge.

      Time
      1.5–2.5 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon for the view and soft light. Come at lunch time if you want seafood in the village.
      Cost
      Free. Leave a small donation if you photograph the reclining Buddha.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Temple open in the daytime. The village is a living community, not an attraction.
      Getting there
      About 4-5 km east of Phuket Old Town, over a very short bridge, about 15 minutes by car or Grab. A small road climbs to the temple; park and walk up the last part. The Urak Lawoi village is at Laem Tukkae, below the temple to the south-west.
      • Cover shoulders and knees in the temple.
      • In the village, be respectful and ask before you take photos of people.
      • Keep food and sunglasses away from the monkeys at the bridge.
      • Hilltop Cafe (a Starbucks) at Sinae Phuket hotel has a 360-degree view, 10:00-20:00. You cannot drive up: buy a 150 THB (≈1,600 AMD) voucher at the base (it pays for one drink) and take the buggy.
      • Thai news reported that a landslide damaged the golden-rock shrine at Wat Koh Sirey (late 2025). Ask locally whether it has reopened.

      Google MapsDirections
      กสิณธร ราชโอรส · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Hidden gem
      30 min–1 h

      Wat Phra Thong (Half-Buried Buddha)

      Thalang · Temple · วัดพระทอง

      Old temple in Thalang with a golden Buddha that comes out of the ground only from the chest up. Local legend says people tried to dig it out but could not. A small museum shows objects from Phuket's tin-mining past. Mostly local people come to pray, so it is calm and real.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Morning, before the heat. Good stop on the way to or from the airport.
      Cost
      Free. Donation boxes.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily, about 08:00-17:30.
      Getting there
      In Thalang, central north Phuket, on a side road off Thepkrasattri Road (the main airport road) near the Thalang crossroads. Coming back from the airport, the side road is on your left; signs are poor. About 20 km from Phuket Town. Car, scooter, taxi or Grab.
      • Cover shoulders and knees. Take off your shoes in the halls.
      • Do not touch or take anything from the ground around the buried Buddha. It is sacred.
      • Wat Phra Nang Sang, one of the oldest temples in Phuket, is about 1 km south-west, on the main road.

      Hidden gem
      1–1.5 h

      Phuket Mining Museum

      Kathu · Culture · พิพิธภัณฑ์เหมืองแร่ภูเก็ต

      Large air-conditioned museum about the tin mines that made Phuket rich long before tourism. It has a mine tunnel section, a big model mine with many small figures and a rebuilt old Phuket street with Chinese merchant life. Some parts look old and worn. Few foreign visitors come.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      A hot or rainy weekday. Arrive before 14:30; it closes at 16:00.
      Cost
      Foreign adult 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD). Child 50-100 THB (≈540-1,100 AMD) (sources differ). Thai adult 50 THB (≈540 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Mon-Sat 09:00-16:00. Sunday is unclear: Google lists Sun 10:00-16:00 and one 2026 guide says daily, but Phuket 101 (Mar 2026) says closed on Sunday. Call 076 322 137 before a Sunday visit. · Only Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat
      Getting there
      Behind Loch Palm Golf Club, on the Kathu - Ko Kaeo road, in the hills between Patong and Phuket Town. The access road is rough in places. Car, scooter or taxi.
      • Allow 1 to 1.5 hours.
      • Part of the visit is outside. Bring a hat and water.
      • Kathu village nearby has old Chinese shrines and is a quiet, local place to walk.

      Hidden gem
      1–1.5 h

      Soi Dog Foundation Sanctuary

      Mai Khao · Activity

      Large shelter for street dogs and cats, run by a well-known charity. A free 45-minute guided tour explains their work and introduces some of the 1,800 animals in their care. After the tour you can spend time in the puppy area and the cat house. Tours are in English and Thai.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Arrive by 10:30 for the morning tour or by 13:30 for the afternoon tour.
      Cost
      Free. Donations and shop purchases help the animals.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Mon-Fri 09:30-11:30 and 13:00-15:30. Free guided tours at 10:30 and 13:30 (45 minutes). Closed Saturday and Sunday. · Only Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri
      Getting there
      Mai Khao, north Phuket, close to the airport. Address: 167/9 Moo 4, Soi Mai Khao 10. Taxi or car; the website has the address in Thai for drivers.
      • No booking needed, but arrive on time for the full tour. Outside tour times the tour may be shorter and skip the puppies.
      • You cannot walk around alone. Stay with the guide.
      • The puppy area or cat house can close at short notice for quarantine.
      • Combine with plane spotting at Mai Khao Beach, a few minutes away.
      • In your dates it is open on weekdays: Fri 8, Mon 11 to Fri 15, Mon 18 to Fri 22, and Mon 25 and Tue 26 January.
      • Flight day, Tue 26 Jan: the 10:30 tour or the 13:30 tour (ends about 14:15) both fit. The terminal is 15-20 minutes away, so you are there before 15:00.
      • With luggage, come in a car that waits for you, or first leave your bags at the AIRPORTELs counter in the terminal (150 baht, ≈1,600 AMD per bag).
      Visitor and tour information (official) ↗

      Hidden gem
      Evening

      Karon Temple Market

      Karon · Market · วัดสุวรรณคีรีเขต (วัดกะรน)

      Twice-a-week night market around Karon's old temple. Many street food stalls: pad thai, grilled skewers, chicken rice, mango sticky rice and fruit shakes. Also cheap clothes, carved soaps and souvenirs. Busy and fun, with a beautiful temple behind the stalls.

      Time
      Evening
      Best time
      Tuesday or Friday from about 16:30-17:00, before the biggest crowds.
      Cost
      Free entry. Cheap street-food prices.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Tuesday and Friday, 16:00-22:00. · Only Tue, Fri
      Getting there
      On the grounds of Wat Karon (Wat Suwan Khiri Khet), Patak Road, about 500 m from the Karon Circle at the back of Karon Beach. Walk from Karon or take a short ride from Kata.
      • Try the pad thai from the stall at the temple entrance. It is the most famous one.
      • Bring small cash notes.
      • Parking is hard. Walk if you stay in Karon, or use the paid car park at the nearby school.
      • In your dates it runs on Fri 8, Tue 12, Fri 15, Tue 19 and Fri 22 January.

      Google MapsDirections
      Sharon Hahn Darlin · CC BY 2.0
      Hidden gem
      Half day

      Blue Elephant Cooking School (Phuket Old Town)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Activity

      A Thai cooking class in a restored governor's mansion, more than 100 years old, in Phuket Old Town. You cook 4-5 dishes in half a day, then eat them in the restaurant. The morning class starts with a visit to a local market. The afternoon class adds a Thai dessert. The dishes change every day.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      The morning class (9:30), because it includes the market visit. Book ahead online.
      Cost
      Group class 3,800 THB (≈41,000 AMD) per person, morning or afternoon. Private teacher, half day: 8,300 THB (≈89,600 AMD) (official booking system, Oct 2026).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Classes every day: morning class 9:30-13:15 with a market visit, afternoon class 13:30-17:00 with an extra Thai dessert (official booking system). Restaurant: daily 11:30-22:00 (Google).
      Getting there
      96 Krabi Road, Phuket Old Town. From Patong about 30 min, from Kamala about 40-45 min, by car or Grab.
      • Check the weekly menu on the official class page before you book: each weekday has different dishes.
      • Classes are taught in English, Thai, French, Dutch or Chinese.
      • You get an apron, the recipes, a certificate and a bag of Blue Elephant products.
      • Cheaper, more casual option near the beaches: Phuket Thai Cooking Class by Chef VJ in Kata. Its official site lists 1,800-2,500 THB (≈19,400-27,000 AMD) (Oct 2026), with free pickup in some areas if you book direct.
      • Thalang Road and the Old Town shophouses start about 300 m to the east, an easy walk after class.

      Renew Sauna & Ice Bath (Bang Tao)

      Bang Tao, Laguna & Cherngtalay · Wellness

      A modern sauna and ice-bath club near Boat Avenue in Bang Tao, about 10-15 minutes from Kamala. It has a Finnish sauna, a steam room, a hot pool, ice plunges and a large pool, plus a cafe with healthy food. Hot-cold rounds help you recover the day after a party. Only for guests aged 16 and over.

      Time
      2–3 h on site
      Best time
      A slow afternoon on a recovery day. It is open until 23:00, so it also works after dinner.
      Cost
      Day ticket 465 THB (≈5,000 AMD) (official price list, Oct 2026). Food and drinks are extra.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:00-23:00 (Google). Ages 16 and over only.
      Getting there
      On Soi Cherngtalay-Bandon 4, a side street off Bandon-Cherngtalay Road, about 250 m from Boat Avenue, Bang Tao. From Kamala about 10-15 min, from Patong about 30-35 min, by car, scooter or Grab.
      • Do 3-4 rounds: sauna or steam, then the cold tub, then rest. Drink a lot of water.
      • Do not go with alcohol still in your body. Heat and ice water are hard on the heart.
      • Another option: KEDR Spa & Sauna in Si Sunthon (Thalang), a calm, compact place with a sauna, steam room, hot tubs, ice plunges and a rain room. Daily 9:00-24:00, ages 14+.
      • For a Thai massage near Kamala: Oasis Spa (Turquoise Cove Spa, Kamala), daily 10:00-24:00 (Google).
      • Questions: Instagram @renew.sauna.

      Nai Thon Beach

      Nai Thon · Beach

      A quiet, sandy bay of about 1 km between two green headlands, 10-15 minutes from the airport. In the dry season the sea is usually clear and good for swimming. A few small restaurants, a minimart and massage shops are across the beach road. Much calmer than the big west-coast beaches.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Late morning to early afternoon. November to February has the calmest, clearest sea. On your flight day, leave by about 14:45.
      Cost
      Free.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Public beach, always open.
      Getting there
      About 7.4 km (10-15 min by car) south of the airport and 10 min south of Nai Yang. No Smart Bus stop on the beach: use Grab or Bolt.
      • Rip currents can happen, mostly when the waves are big. Swim in the middle of the bay and never at a red flag.
      • Snorkelling is only fair: try the rocks at the headlands on calm days.
      • Bamboo Beach Restaurant (Google 4.7, 186 reviews), at the south end, is open daily 10:00-22:00.
      • Last swim on Tue 26 Jan: leave by about 14:45 and you reach the terminal in 10-15 minutes.

      Sabai Massage & Spa (airport branch)

      Nai Yang · Wellness

      Massage and spa shop near the airport with a very high rating (Google 4.9 from 2,050 reviews). Thai, oil, foot, herbal-compress and head-and-shoulder massages in air-conditioned rooms. A good way to spend the last hours before a long flight, and they can drive you to the terminal.

      Time
      1–2 h on site
      Best time
      After check-out on your last day, for example 13:00-15:00, then the free drop-off to the terminal.
      Cost
      Thai or oil massage from 400-500 THB (≈4,300-5,400 AMD) for 60 min; Thai plus foot massage, 120 min, 800 THB (≈8,600 AMD) (official site, Oct 2026). Free airport drop-off if you spend at least 600 THB (≈6,500 AMD) and book directly 1 day before.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:30-23:30, last booking 22:30 (official site).
      Getting there
      18/18 Moo 1, Sakhu, on the main road about 1 km from the terminal (5 min by car).
      • Book on LINE @sabaimassage or WhatsApp 085-333-6333 the day before, and ask for the free airport drop-off ('while availability lasts').
      • Finish by about 15:00 so you are at the terminal by 15:20.
      • Ask if you can keep your bags next to you during the massage. If not, leave them at the airport left-luggage counter first.
