      Phang Nga Bay: James Bond Island and sea caves

      Phang Nga · Island · อ่าวพังงา เกาะเขาพิงกัน

      A calm bay full of tall limestone islands. Tours stop at James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan and the Ko Tapu rock), take you by canoe into sea caves and hidden lagoons at Panak or Hong island, and stop for lunch at Koh Panyee, a Muslim fishing village on stilts.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      Take an early tour (start 7:00-8:30). Boats crowd the islands 10:00-14:00. December to March is the busiest time.
      Cost
      Group tour 1,400-3,500 THB (≈15,100-37,800 AMD) per person: longtail 1,400-1,600, big boat 1,500-1,800, speedboat 1,800-2,500, catamaran or premium 2,500-3,500. Park fee 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) (Thai National Parks site, 2022 list) or 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD) (Phuket 101, 2026); usually included.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Tours run daily in the dry season. The park is open in January.
      Getting there
      Hotel pickup, then a 45-60 min drive to Ao Po (Ao Por) Pier or Royal Phuket Marina on the east coast. Some longtail tours use Bang Rong Pier. Back at the hotel about 17:00-18:00.
      • You cannot swim at James Bond Island. Tours stop to swim at other islands.
      • In the caves a guide paddles the canoe for you. Check that canoeing is included.
      • At Koh Panyee, walk past the main souvenir walkway to see real village life.
      • Speedboats spend less time on the water and more time at the islands.
      • The Hong by Starlight trip also passes James Bond Island (seen from the boat only), so you may not need both.

      Hong by Starlight: evening sea-canoe trip

      Phang Nga · Activity · เกาะห้อง อ่าวพังงา

      John Gray's Sea Canoe runs this trip from midday into the night. You pass James Bond Island (from the boat), then guides paddle you into sea caves and hidden lagoons at Panak and Hong islands. You make a krathong (small floating offering), eat a Thai buffet at sunset, then paddle in the dark to see glowing plankton.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      Plankton glows best on dark nights. New moon is Fri 8 Jan 2027, so book early in your trip and skip the full-moon days around Fri 22 Jan.
      Cost
      From 3,950 THB (≈42,700 AMD) per adult (official site). Hotel transfer, light lunch, buffet dinner, park fees and travel insurance are included.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily. Pickup about 10:20-11:15, back at the hotel about 21:00-21:30.
      Getting there
      Hotel pickup in Phuket. The boat leaves from Ao Po (Ao Por) Pier in north-east Phuket.
      • The order of stops can change with the tide.
      • Bring swimwear: there is time to paddle and swim in the afternoon.
      • A private-charter version of the same trip is sold from 62,750 THB (≈678,000 AMD).
      • Other companies sell similar sunset canoe and plankton trips from about 3,300 THB (≈35,600 AMD) (for example Tisland 'Shine of Andaman').

      Phi Phi Islands and Maya Bay

      Phi Phi · Island · หมู่เกาะพีพี อ่าวมาหยา

      The famous islands 45-60 min by speedboat from Phuket. Tours visit Maya Bay (from the film The Beach), Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, snorkel spots and often Bamboo Island. At Maya Bay boats stop at a pier in Loh Samah Bay and you walk in. Swimming is banned there: knee-deep wading only.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      Choose an early-departure or sunrise tour to reach Maya Bay before the main crowds.
      Cost
      Group speedboat tour about 1,500-3,500 THB (≈16,200-37,800 AMD); sunrise tours 3,500-4,500 THB (≈37,800-48,600 AMD). Park fee 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD) (child 200); sometimes not included, so ask. Private speedboat 15,000-25,000 THB (≈162,000-270,000 AMD) per boat.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Maya Bay about 07:00-18:00. Closed every year 1 Aug - 30 Sep, so it is open in January.
      Getting there
      Hotel pickup 6:30-7:30 to Rassada Pier (Phuket Town) or Royal Phuket Marina. Back about 16:00-17:00. Public ferry Rassada - Tonsai about 2 h, about 600 THB (≈6,500 AMD) one way.
      • Maya Bay takes up to 375 people per hour. Expect 30-60 minutes on the beach.
      • Sunscreen with oxybenzone, octinoxate, 4MBC or butylparaben is banned in Thai national parks (fines up to 100,000 THB, ≈1,080,000 AMD).
      • For seasickness, take a pill 30 minutes before and sit at the back of the boat.
      • If you stay a night on Phi Phi Don, the last ferry back to Phuket is about 15:30.

      Similan Islands

      Phang Nga · Island · หมู่เกาะสิมิลัน

      A national park of granite islands about 60 km off the Khao Lak coast, with the clearest water and best snorkelling near Phuket. You climb Sail Rock on Island 8 for the famous view of Donald Duck Bay, snorkel between islands and have lunch on Island 4. Open 15 Oct 2026 to 15 May 2027.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      January is ideal for sea and sun but very busy. Take an early-departure tour.
      Cost
      Day tour from Phuket about 2,500-3,800 THB (≈27,000-41,000 AMD) with transfer, lunch and park fee. Park fee alone: 500 THB (≈5,400 AMD) (child 250), as an e-ticket.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Season 15 Oct 2026 - 15 May 2027. Day visits only: no overnight stays.
      Getting there
      Long day. Hotel pickup about 06:00-07:00 (early tours 03:00-04:30), then 1-1.5 h by van to Thap Lamu Pier (Khao Lak) and 60-90 min by speedboat. Back in Phuket in the evening.
      • Only 3,325 day visitors (plus 525 divers) are allowed per day, shared by all tour companies. Book ahead.
      • Avoid the cheapest speedboats: they are crowded. Mid-range boats have shade and space.
      • Do not feed fish and do not stand on coral.
      • The ride is much shorter if you stay in Khao Lak.

      Koh Racha Yai

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Island · เกาะราชาใหญ่

      A hilly island 30-45 min by speedboat south of Phuket, with white sand and very clear water. Day boats land at Patok Bay, where you can snorkel straight from the beach. A short walk leads to quieter Siam Bay. Many tours combine Racha with Coral Island.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      November to April has calm sea and clear water. Day boats arrive from about 10:00. The island empties around 16:00.
      Cost
      Racha + Coral speedboat tour from about 1,300 THB (≈14,000 AMD) per person with lunch. No national park fee.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Getting there
      Hotel pickup 7:00-9:00 to Chalong Pier, then speedboat 30-45 min (big boats 60-90 min). Back at the pier about 15:30-16:30.
      • Bring a towel: Patok Bay has no public sunbeds.
      • Bring your own mask if you have one. Rental masks often leak.
      • Stay a night at a Patok Bay resort to have the beach almost to yourself after 16:00.
      • Divers: manta rays pass Racha Noi from January to March.

      Coral Island (Koh Hey)

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Island · เกาะเฮ

      A small island only 15 min by speedboat from Chalong or Rawai. Most boats land at busy Long Beach with restaurants, sunbeds and water sports. Banana Beach, further east, is quieter and is mostly visited with its own day packages. Easy snorkelling near the shore. A short and cheap escape.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      November to April has the calmest water. Long Beach is busiest from late morning to early afternoon.
      Cost
      Free entry. Speedboat tour with lunch 1,100-2,200 THB (≈11,900-23,800 AMD) per person. Banana Beach packages from 1,900 THB (≈20,500 AMD). Longtail from Rawai 1,500-2,000 THB (≈16,200-21,600 AMD) per boat. Sunbeds and water sports cost extra.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Getting there
      Speedboat from Chalong Pier or Rawai Beach (about 15 min), or a shared or private longtail from Rawai.
      • For a quieter beach, book a boat or package that lands at Banana Beach.
      • Often sold together with Racha Yai as one full-day trip.

      Khai Islands (Koh Khai Nok)

      Phang Nga · Island · เกาะไข่นอก

      Three tiny islands 15-20 min by speedboat from Phuket's east coast. Khai Nok has a white beach with bars and sunbeds. Khai Nai is the largest, with long, shallow sand. Khai Nui has no beach but the best reef: you snorkel from the boat. Short, easy and cheap, but always busy.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Leave early in the morning, before the tour groups. November to April is calmest.
      Cost
      Half-day speedboat tour about 1,100 THB (≈11,900 AMD) (child 900), with transfer, snorkel gear and entry fees. Full day with another island about 1,250 THB (≈13,500 AMD). Private speedboat 2,500-5,000 THB (≈27,000-54,000 AMD). Sunbeds 150 THB (≈1,600 AMD) for two, free with a food order.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Getting there
      Hotel pickup to Chalong Pier, Ao Po Pier or Royal Phuket Marina, then 15-20 min by speedboat.
      • Feeding fish is banned. Rangers give fines.
      • Keep your life jacket on at Khai Nui: the current can be strong.
      • Boats skip Khai Nui when the sea is rough.

      Koh Yao Noi

      Koh Yao · Island · เกาะยาวน้อย

      A quiet, green island in Phang Nga Bay, 30 min by speedboat from Phuket. Rent a scooter, ride past rice fields and small villages, swim at Pasai or Klong Jark beach and kayak to Koh Nok. Views over the limestone islands of the bay. Mostly Muslim and not a party island: a real break.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      Take the first boat (08:40). Better: stay one or two nights.
      Cost
      Speedboat about 300-500 THB (≈3,200-5,400 AMD) per person each way (price differs by seller and online). Slow longtail about 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD). Scooter 250-350 THB (≈2,700-3,800 AMD) a day. Kayak about 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) for a few hours.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Speedboats from Bang Rong Pier about 08:40-17:00 (longtail 12:30). Boats back from Manoh Pier about 06:35-16:00: the last one is about 16:00.
      Getting there
      Grab or taxi to Bang Rong Pier (north-east Phuket, about 22 km and 40 min from the airport). Speedboat 30-40 min, or the slow longtail at 12:30 (1 h), to Manoh Pier. Taxis and songthaews wait at the pier.
      • Dress modestly in the villages. Not every shop sells alcohol.
      • Kayak to Koh Nok early, at high tide. The afternoon sea is choppy.
      • Koh Hong (Krabi) is about 20 min by longtail from Klong Jark Beach (about 800 THB, ≈8,600 AMD per person in 2024).
      • Bring enough cash. ATMs can run out on busy weekends.
      • Phuket 101 says two nights is the minimum to enjoy the island.

      Koh Hong (Krabi): lagoon island

      Krabi · Island · เกาะห้อง กระบี่

      A limestone island between Koh Yao Noi and Krabi. Boats go into a shallow lagoon ringed by tall cliffs, and there are two white-sand beaches with clear water. Steep stairs lead to a viewpoint. It is part of a national park and is busy from late morning.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      Go early. Tour boats from Krabi arrive in the late morning.
      Cost
      Park fee 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) per adult, cash, paid at the floating pier. From Koh Yao Noi: longtail about 800 THB (≈8,600 AMD) per person (2024). From Krabi or Ao Nang: group speedboat tours about 1,350-1,500 THB (≈14,600-16,200 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Getting there
      From Phuket, some speedboat island tours include Hong (Krabi); ask for it by name. Or stay on Koh Yao Noi and take a longtail (about 20 min) from Klong Jark Beach.
      • No alcohol and no drones on the island.
      • Expect a long, bouncy floating pier to reach the beach.
      • Koh Pakbia, nearby, is a good picnic stop.
      • Do not mix it up with Koh Hong in Phang Nga Bay (Hong by Starlight trip).

      Railay Beach (Krabi)

      Krabi · Beach · ไร่เลย์

      A beach area in Krabi with no roads, closed in by huge limestone cliffs, so you arrive by boat. West Railay is a beautiful sunset beach and Phra Nang Cave Beach is close by. Famous for rock climbing. A direct ferry from Phuket makes a long day trip possible, but one or two nights is better.

      Time
      Full day
      Best time
      For a day trip take the first ferry. If you stay, watch sunset at West Railay (about 18:25 in mid-January).
      Cost
      Ferry Phuket - Railay about 660-1,360 THB (≈7,100-14,700 AMD) one way (EUR 17.65-36 online, Oct 2026).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Ferries leave Rassada Pier 08:30-12:00 (1 h 20 min - 2 h 30 min). Back from Railay 12:45-15:15.
      Getting there
      Ferry from Rassada Pier (Phuket Town) to Railay East floating pier, then a short walk to West Railay. Longtails link Railay with Ao Nang and Krabi Town.
      • Book the ferry early: online prices rise close to the date.
      • Be at the pier 60 minutes before departure.
      • There are no night ferries back to Phuket.

      Khao Sok: Cheow Lan Lake overnight

      Nature · เขื่อนเชี่ยวหลาน

      A huge jungle lake with limestone cliffs in Khao Sok National Park. Longtail boats take you from the dam pier to floating raft houses. You sleep on the water, swim, and kayak in the morning mist. A 1-day tour exists but is very long (about 15 hours), so one night is better.

      Time
      2+ days
      Best time
      January to March is the dry season.
      Cost
      1-day tour from Phuket from 3,500 THB (≈37,800 AMD); 2 days / 1 night from 7,900 THB (≈85,300 AMD) (park fees included). Lake fee alone: 300 THB (≈3,200 AMD) (child 150).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Boats run only between sunrise and sunset.
      Getting there
      Tour pickup in Phuket 05:00-06:30. The 1-day tour reaches the lake about 10:00 and is back about 19:30-20:30. The pier is about 155 km by road from Phuket Airport (about 3 h). All boats leave from Ratchaprapha Pier at the dam.
      • Some raft houses are up to 1 h 20 min by boat from the pier.
      • Basic raft houses often have power only in the evening.
      • Boats are limited in high season, so book ahead.
      • On the lake, mobile signal works mainly on AIS.

      Samet Nangshe viewpoint (sunrise)

      Phang Nga · Viewpoint · จุดชมวิวเสม็ดนางชี

      A hilltop viewpoint over Phang Nga Bay: green mangroves and dozens of limestone islands in the morning mist. Come for sunrise. From the car park you walk up about 20 minutes or take a pickup truck. There are two viewpoints on the way up.

      Time
      Half day
      Best time
      Arrive by 05:30-06:00. Sunrise in January is about 06:45; the sky gets light from about 06:20.
      Cost
      30 THB (≈320 AMD) on foot, 90 THB (≈970 AMD) return by pickup truck (entry included). Sunrise tour from Phuket about 2,200-2,400 THB (≈23,800-25,900 AMD).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Opens about 05:00-05:30 every day.
      Getting there
      About 50 km (1 h) by car from Phuket Airport, about 80 km (1.5-2 h) from Patong. Cross the Sarasin Bridge and drive north to Takua Thung. Sunrise tours pick up about 04:00.
      • Private cars must stop at the bottom car park. Google Maps' main pin is this car park and truck stop.
      • Wear real shoes and bring water. The path is steep and has no shade.
      • Sleep at the top in a tent (about 130 THB, ≈1,400 AMD) or a bungalow (500-700 THB, ≈5,400-7,600 AMD) to skip the night drive.
      • The small platforms fill up fast on clear mornings, especially at weekends.

      Koh Phangan rave trip (2-5 days)

      Koh Phangan · Nightlife · เกาะพะงัน

      Thailand's party island, in the Gulf. Most jungle raves are inland near Ban Tai. With the group: OXA (Fri 8 and 15 Jan), Lost Jungle psytrance (Sat 9 to Mon 11) and Halfmoon (Fri 15 - Sat 16). In full-moon week: OXA (Tue 19), Waterfall (Wed 20), Jungle Experience (Thu 21) and the Full Moon Party (Fri 22 Jan).

      Time
      2+ days
      Best time
      Two good windows. With the group: Sun 10 to Wed 13 Jan (Lost Jungle until 11 Jan, Chill Up on Mon 11, the Lighthouse Party on Tue 12). For the two of you: Tue 19 to Sat 23 Jan, the full-moon week, then fly back for the last Circoloco on Sat 23. See Info, Koh Phangan full-moon week.
      Cost
      Flight Phuket - Samui about 3,000 to 5,000 THB (≈32,400 to 54,000 AMD) one way, plus the boat. Bus + boat about 700-1,600 THB (≈7,600-17,300 AMD). Party tickets: OXA from 500 THB (≈5,400 AMD); Halfmoon about 1,500-3,500 THB (≈16,200-37,800 AMD) at the gate (online often a bit less).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Getting there
      Fastest: Bangkok Airways Phuket - Koh Samui (about 1 h, 8 flights a day; take one at 14:15 or earlier to catch the boats), then a 20-60 min boat (Lomprayah or Seatran) to Thong Sala Pier. Budget: bus + boat via Don Sak, about 6-9 h (Lomprayah 07:00-12:45 or 09:30-16:30 in Oct 2026).
      • Bring cash. Party bars are cash only and OXA has no ATM.
      • Bring your passport: Halfmoon checks ID, and some ticket sites say 20+.
      • Eden Garden on Haad Yuan has deep house and techno on Saturdays. Taxi boat from Haad Rin about 400 THB (≈4,300 AMD).
      • Night taxis charge per car, so share a ride.
      • Small underground nights post dates only 1-3 weeks ahead. Check RA and phangan.events in December.
      • Full-moon week (20-24 Jan): rooms cost 2-3 times more and many ask for a 3-5 night minimum. Book in October or November. Ban Tai is the best base.

      Rawai Seafood Market

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Food · ตลาดทะเลสด หาดราไวย์

      A 100 m strip next to Rawai Pier, in an old sea gypsy fishing village. Fish stalls are on one side, restaurants on the other. You choose fish, prawns, crab or lobster, pay by weight, and a restaurant across the road cooks it your way. Fun, but no longer cheap.

      Time
      1.5–2 h on site
      Best time
      Around 18:00-19:00 for dinner and a lively scene. Late morning is quietest.
      Cost
      Seafood is priced per kg (large prawns up to about 1,500 THB, ≈16,200 AMD/kg). Cooking fee about 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) per kg, or 50-100 THB (≈540-1,100 AMD) per dish.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily. Google lists 9:00-21:00, Phuket 101 says 11:00-21:00. Mook Manee, the biggest restaurant, is open 11:30-22:00.
      Getting there
      On Wiset Road next to Rawai Pier. About 35-45 min from Patong, 15-25 min from Kata.
      • Agree the price per kg before they bag it, and watch the scale.
      • Ask the cooking fee first: some places charge per kg, others per dish.
      • Bring cash for the stalls.
      • Mook Manee, between the pier and the market, is the biggest restaurant here and is listed in the Michelin Guide.

      1–1.5 h

      One Chun

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · วันจันทร์

      Phuket family recipes in an old Old Town shophouse with vintage decor. Order the crab meat yellow curry with rice noodles, moo hong (sweet braised pork belly) and fried prawns in tamarind sauce. Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Lunch, then walk around the Old Town.
      Cost
      Dishes about 120-390 THB (≈1,300-4,200 AMD) (crab curry 390, moo hong 265; 2024 menu).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      10:00-22:00 daily (Tue until 21:00).
      • Raya, the famous older restaurant with the same Phuket dishes, is a few steps away at 48/1 Dibuk Road (Google lists 11:00-21:00). Its main rooms have no air-con, and it left the Michelin guide in 2026.
      • Ask for less spicy if you are not used to Thai chili.
      One Chun (MICHELIN Guide) ↗One Chun on Instagram ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © Meetonpoe (Mee Ton Poe) · official site
      Food
      30 min–1 h

      Mee Ton Poe (Hokkien noodles)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · หมี่ต้นโพธิ์

      Phuket's best-known Hokkien noodle shop, cooking since 1946 at the clock tower circle in Phuket Town. The classic is mee Hokkien: thick yellow noodles fried with pork, seafood and greens in a rich gravy, topped with a soft egg. Add pork satay. Simple, fast and cheap.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Breakfast or lunch.
      Cost
      Cheap: mee Hokkien with egg about 80 THB (≈860 AMD), Phuket fish balls 80 THB (≈860 AMD), hor mok 20 THB (≈220 AMD) (Wongnai review, Mar 2026).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Phuket Town shop 09:30-18:30 daily.
      • One plate is usually enough. Order a second if you are hungry.
      • The shop next door serves the same noodles as a soup.
      • Other branches: Mee Ton Poe 2 in Kathu and Mee Ton Poe 4 on Thep Krasattri Road in Thalang (both open until about 20:00).
      Mee Ton Poe on Facebook ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      JULIANISME · CC BY-SA 4.0
      Food
      1–1.5 h

      Malin Plaza night market (Patong)

      Patong & Kalim · Food · มาลิน พลาซ่า

      A big covered night market at the south end of Patong. The front half is food: grills, seafood on ice that they cook for you, pad thai, fruit, pancakes and mango sticky rice, with shared tables. The back half sells clothes and souvenirs. Touristy and warm (no air-con), but cheap for Patong.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      18:00-19:00: stalls are ready and tables are free. Busiest 20:00-22:00, peak around 21:00.
      Cost
      Free entry. Street dishes about 80-120 THB (≈860-1,300 AMD) (pad thai 80, pad kra pao 100-120). Seafood is by weight: ask the total before they cook it.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 11:00-23:00. Almost empty until late afternoon.
      Getting there
      South end of Patong on Prachanukhro Road, 1.6 km from Bangla Road (about 20 minutes on foot). Tuk-tuk from central or north Patong about 200 THB (≈2,200 AMD), or use Grab. Parking is hard: a scooter is fine, a car is not.
      • Bargain for souvenirs, not for food. A cap offered at 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD) sold for 70 THB (≈760 AMD).
      • Look at a few food stalls first: a few charge more than the others.
      • Halal food: several stalls show it on the sign. Check each stall.
      • Some sellers in the shopping half are pushy. A smile and a 'no' works.

      Google MapsDirections
      © Willy Thuan / phuket101.net · © phuket101.net (third-party site, all rights reserved)
      Food
      1.5–3 h

      Kruvit Raft (Floating Seafood Restaurant)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · แพครูวิทย์

      Big wooden raft restaurant on the sea between Phuket and Koh Maphrao, listed in the 2026 Michelin Guide. Fish, crabs, prawns and oysters live in nets under the deck. You point at what you want and they cook it. Most guests are Thai. A fun and very local seafood meal.

      Time
      1.5–3 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon, so you see the bay in daylight. Sunset is about 18:30 in January.
      Cost
      Free boat. Most seafood is priced by weight (per 100 g); mid to upper local prices.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:00-22:00.
      Getting there
      Drive to Laem Hin Pier, about 10 km north of Phuket Town: take the airport road and turn right onto the small road to Laem Hin. Look for the Kruvit sign. A free longtail boat takes you to the raft in about 5 minutes.
      • For directions, navigate to Laem Hin Pier (ท่าเรือแหลมหิน), not to the raft. The raft is on the water.
      • Ask the weight and price before they cook lobster or mantis shrimp.
      • Try blue crab, grilled king prawns and the sour fish soup with soybean (Pla Tom Towchiew).
      • Bring cash; cards do not always work on the raft. A 20-50 THB (≈220-540 AMD) tip for the boatman on the way back is welcome.
      • Book for weekend evenings. Weekday lunch is usually fine without booking.
      Michelin Guide listing ↗

      Google MapsDirections to Laem Hin Pier
      © Summore Day Phuket (official Instagram @summoreday) · official site (cafe's Instagram)
      Food
      1–2 h

      Summore Day Cafe

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep · Food

      Hillside cafe, restaurant and bar with terraced gardens, a koi pond and a rooftop deck over Ya Nui Beach and Koh Man island. Serious coffee from their own roast, food from breakfast to steak, and cocktails with local Chalong Bay rum. Live music on weekend afternoons.

      Time
      1–2 h on site
      Best time
      Late afternoon before sunset. Weekdays are quieter.
      Cost
      Coffee 100-220 THB (≈1,100-2,400 AMD), mains 320-790 THB (≈3,500-8,500 AMD), cocktails 320-420 THB (≈3,500-4,500 AMD) (2026 menu).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:00-20:00. Last food order about 19:00. Live music on weekend afternoons from about 14:30.
      Getting there
      On the coast road between Ya Nui Beach and Promthep Cape, just below the cape car park. Free parking at the entrance.
      • Order and pay at the counter inside, then sit anywhere.
      • Use mosquito spray at dusk in the garden.
      • After coffee, go up to Promthep Cape for the sunset.
      Facebook (official) ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © Willy Thuan / phuket101.net · © phuket101.net (third-party site, all rights reserved)
      Food
      1–1.5 h

      View Cafe at Phuket (Phuket View Coffee and Resort)

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad · Food

      Quiet hilltop cafe high above Bang Wad Reservoir. From terraces and small balconies you look over Phuket Town, the east coast, Chalong Bay and the islands. Simple Thai food, coffee and cold drinks. No tour buses; most guests are locals. Best on a clear day.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      A clear afternoon. Late afternoon light over Phuket Town is best.
      Cost
      Simple Thai food, coffee and cold drinks. Prices not published.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 09:00-19:30 (Google lists Fri-Sun until 20:00).
      Getting there
      In the hills between Chalong and Kathu, above Bang Wad Reservoir, near the Phuket weather station. Address: 56 Chalong 10, Moo 5, Ban Nai Trok Road. The road is narrow, steep and winding; car or scooter only.
      • Take an outdoor table for the best view. There is also an air-conditioned room.
      • Ride slowly. The road up is steep and narrow.
      • It also rents a few rooms if you want to stay the night.
      Official website ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      Streets of Food (www.streetsoffood.com), via Flickr · CC BY 2.0
      Food
      30 min–1 h

      Lock Tien (Phuket street dishes)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · ลกเที้ยน

      A Phuket Town classic for local Hokkien-Chinese dishes in one place: fried Hokkien noodles, fresh spring rolls (popia sot), o-tao (taro and oyster omelette), lo ba (fried pork and tofu) and o-aew jelly dessert. It has moved from its old corner food court to a shophouse on Bangkok Road.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Lunch or an afternoon snack.
      Cost
      Cheap local prices (dish prices not published).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      09:00-19:00 daily.
      • Old maps still show the closed food court on Yaowarat Road. Go to 59/14 Bangkok Road, opposite the Government Housing Bank.
      • Paid parking (20 THB, ≈220 AMD) opposite the bank, or free spaces on Bangkok Road.
      • It is now one kitchen with one menu, not separate stalls. Point at the photos on the awning to order.

      Google MapsDirections
      lin Judy (快樂雲), via Flickr · CC BY-NC-ND 2.0
      Food
      30 min–1 h

      Go Benz (late-night rice soup)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · โกเบนซ์ ข้าวต้มแห้ง

      A corner shop open at night, known for kuay jap (rolled rice noodles in peppery pork broth) and khao tom (rice soup), with crispy pork belly on the side. Open until about 1:30 at night, so it is perfect after a party. Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2019.

      Time
      30 min–1 h on site
      Best time
      Peak is 19:00-21:00 with a 20-30 min queue. Quieter after 21:30 and after midnight.
      Cost
      Dishes 50-90 THB (≈540-970 AMD) (rice soup or kuay jap 50, crispy pork 60-90). Drinks 20 THB (≈220 AMD). Cash only.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Tue-Sun 17:00-01:30. Closed Mon and on Buddhist holy days (in your dates: Fri 15 and Fri 22 Jan).
      • Take any free seat; staff come to take your order.
      • The dry rice soup with crispy pork and offal often sells out.
      • Parking is hard. Come by Grab or taxi.
      Go Benz (MICHELIN Guide) ↗Go Benz on Facebook ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © MICHELIN Guide · MICHELIN Guide photo (personal use)
      Food
      1–1.5 h

      Naam Yoi (Southern Thai curries)

      Phuket Town (Old Town) · Food · ร้านน้ำย้อย

      A small, simple local place known for rich, very aromatic Southern Thai curries, cooked to order with produce bought at dawn. Try kaeng som (sour fish curry with tamarind) and kaeng pa (jungle curry). No English menu and plastic chairs, but real local flavour. Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Lunch.
      Cost
      Cheap local prices (no dish prices published). Order several dishes to share.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:30-14:15 and 16:30-19:15 (weekends until 14:00 and 19:00).
      • Hard to find: it is behind tall bushes on a small back road.
      • They can make dishes less spicy if you ask.
      • Backup: Ko Tee Sangkasi Restaurant on Yaowarat Road, about 3 km west (Tue-Sun 09:00-20:00, cash only, about 150 THB, ≈1,600 AMD a dish) for sour curries and crab curry.
      Naam Yoi (MICHELIN Guide) ↗Naam Yoi on Facebook ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © MICHELIN Guide · MICHELIN Guide photo (personal use)
      Food
      1.5–2 h

      Mor Mu Dong (mangrove seafood)

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad · Food · หมอมูดง

      Southern Thai food in open wooden huts over a mangrove canal near Chalong, about 10 km from Phuket Town. Mostly local diners. Live seafood waits in tanks by the open kitchen. Try stuffed mackerel, salt-fried pork, sea grape salad, lime squid and salt-crusted fish. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

      Time
      1.5–2 h on site
      Best time
      Weekdays are calmer. On weekends arrive before 12:00: the car park fills and you take a queue number. High tide gives the best view (check a tide app). At low tide you see mud and small red crabs.
      Cost
      Most dishes 100-200 THB (≈1,100-2,200 AMD); whole fish by weight. About 300-500 THB (≈3,200-5,400 AMD) per person. Cards are listed as accepted, but bring cash as backup.
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 10:00-21:00. Closed on the 15th of every month (on your trip: Fri 15 Jan).
      Getting there
      Car, scooter or Grab. About 20-25 min from Phuket Town (10 km), 25-30 min from Kata (11 km) and 35-45 min from Patong (20 km). It is at the end of a small road in the mangroves. Google Maps finds it easily.
      • Order the salt-crusted fish (pla pao) first. It takes about 30 minutes.
      • No reservations. On busy days you take a number and wait. Ask for a hut over the water.
      • In the huts you sit on the floor at a low table. Some bigger huts, and the tables under the trees, have chairs.
      • The menu has photos of every dish, so you can point.
      • Backup on the 15th or when it is full: Chaiyo Seafood Restaurant (daily 10:30-21:30). It is across the canal, but about 10 km by road.
      Mor Mu Dong (MICHELIN Guide) ↗Mor Mu Dong (Facebook) ↗

      Google MapsDirections
      © Natural Restaurant (ครัวธรรมชาติ) · official site
      Food
      1–1.5 h

      Natural Restaurant (airport branch)

      Nai Yang · Food

      Family-run Southern Thai restaurant since 1992, in a tropical garden with a waterfall. The long picture menu has fresh Andaman seafood such as fish and prawns, curries made with house curry pastes, and spicy salads. Air-conditioned rooms too. A relaxed last meal close to the airport.

      Time
      1–1.5 h on site
      Best time
      Lunch on your last day, about 12:00-13:30. It is 5 minutes from the terminal.
      Cost
      Mid-range prices (the restaurant's own price level is ฿฿). Pay by cash, card or Thai QR (PromptPay).
      Opening, getting there & tips
      Open
      Daily 07:00-00:30 (official site and Google Maps, Oct 2026).
      Getting there
      3/10 Moo 1, Baan Nai Yang, Sakhu: about 2-3 km from the international terminal (the restaurant says 3.2 km), about 5 minutes by car or Grab. Free parking.
      • Google 4.7 from more than 3,000 reviews, so it is busy at lunch. Book on Chope (link on the official site) or come before 12:00.
      • In Google Maps, pick the 'Natural Restaurant' at 3/10 Moo 1, Baan Nai Yang, Sakhu. The other Natural Restaurant is in Phuket Town.
      • Ask for the Southern Thai dishes and say how spicy you want them.
      Official site ↗

      Where to base yourself

      Areas of Phuket

      Tap an area on the map to read about it. The colors match the cards below. For this trip the best base is Kamala, with a driver for the Circoloco nights in Natai.

      For you

      Best bases for this trip

      Main base: Kamala, at the quiet north end. You can walk to Café del Mar, and Shelter in Patong is about 20 minutes by car. Bang Tao is the same idea with more restaurants, but it is farther from Patong.

      For the Circoloco Saturdays (9, 16 and 23 Jan), book a driver both ways: Natai is about 1 hour from Kamala. Sleeping in Natai is hard on those nights: Baba Beach Club has no rooms on sale for 8 to 27 Jan, Natai House showed no rooms online for 9 and 16 Jan, and Aleenta costs about 45,000 to 52,000 THB (≈486,000 to 562,000 AMD) per night then.

      With the group: Kamala 8 to 18 Jan (Koh Phangan 10 to 13 Jan if you go). The two of you: Ban Tai on Koh Phangan, 19 to 23 Jan. From Sat 23 Jan: near the airport in Nai Yang, 35 to 45 minutes from Natai after Circoloco and 5 to 10 minutes from the terminal on flight day.

      Want these areas inside Google Maps? Download the KML file, then on a computer open Google My Maps → Create a new map → Import. The map then shows in the Google Maps app under Saved → Maps.

      Patong & Kalim

      Party town, with real techno in Shelter at Illuzion

      nightlifetechnobeach clubsshoppingbudgetmuay thai

      Phuket's busiest and loudest area. Bangla Road closes to cars from 18:00 and fills with bars, go-go bars and big clubs. Illuzion is number 9 in DJ Mag's Top 100 Clubs 2026; its Shelter room plays techno and minimal. Hotels for every budget and street food. Kalim, just north, is a quieter rocky bay with good restaurants.

      Stay here if you want to walk to Shelter and Illuzion and do not mind noise; sleep at the north end or in Kalim.

      Kamala

      Calm family beach with Café del Mar at the north end

      beach clubsbeachswimmingfamiliescouplessunset

      A long, wide beach by a Muslim fishing village, calmer and more Thai than Patong. Families, couples and repeat visitors like it. Café del Mar at the quiet north end books big house and techno DJs in season. Apart from Café del Mar, nights are quiet; Phuket FantaSea and Carnival Magic are the big evening shows.

      Stay here if you want a calm beach, Café del Mar on foot, and Shelter and Enthusiast Place within about 20 minutes by car.

      Surin & Pansea

      One of Phuket's best beaches, now with nothing on the sand

      beachswimmingluxurycouplesquietsunset

      An 800 m bay of soft pale sand between Kamala and Bang Tao, with casuarina trees behind it. All food stalls, sunbeds and massages were removed in May 2025, so it looks natural again. Tukta, on the rocks at the south end, is one of only two places still serving food. Twinpalms, The Surin and Amanpuri are close.

      Stay here if you want a quiet luxury hotel on a beautiful beach and will take taxis for food and parties.

      Bang Tao, Laguna & Cherngtalay

      Long beach, top restaurants and beach clubs

      foodbeach clubsluxuryfamilieslong staybeach

      A 6 km beach with the Laguna resort complex in the middle and Cherngtalay town behind it. The upmarket side of Phuket: villas, Michelin-listed restaurants and Boat Avenue's shops and bars. Catch and Xana are the big beach clubs. Traffic is often bad.

      Stay here if you want great food and beach clubs nearby and a 30-minute ride to the airport, and do not need a party street.

      Layan

      Quiet north end of Bang Tao with an island and a river

      quietluxurycouplesbeachnature

      The quiet north end of Bang Tao Bay, inside Sirinat National Park. The beach ends at a river mouth with a big wooded island in front. The small restaurants under the trees were removed; only Tan Restaurant & Massage is left. Anantara Layan and other luxury villas sit just north of the river. Very quiet at night.

      Stay here if you want a peaceful villa or resort near the airport and Bang Tao, and will take taxis for nights out.

      Nai Thon

      Quiet bay under green hills, 15 minutes from the airport

      quietswimmingbeachnaturecouplesairport

      A small curved bay below steep hills, inside Sirinat National Park. There is no real town, just a few hotels, guesthouses and simple Thai restaurants along the beach. Quiet day and night. Banana Beach, 2 km south, changed in late 2025: the old jungle path closed, and a car park (100 THB, ≈1,100 AMD) and a big beach club opened.

      Stay here if you want a quiet beach close to the airport for your first or last nights.

      Nai Yang

      Beach restaurants and planes, 10 minutes from the airport

      airportlocal lifefoodfamiliesnaturebudget

      A relaxed beach village next to the airport, inside Sirinat National Park. Casuarina trees give shade, and simple restaurants put tables on the sand. It has an old-Phuket feel. There is a coral reef off the beach, and the plane-spotting spot at the end of the runway is close. Nightlife is a few small bars.

      Stay here if you have an early flight or want simple beach food and a local feel near the airport.

      Mai Khao

      11 km of empty sand, big resorts and landing planes

      luxuryquietnaturefamiliescouplesairport

      Phuket's longest beach, 11 km, inside Sirinat National Park. No chairs, vendors or jet skis, just a few big resorts set back from the sand, such as Sala, Renaissance, JW Marriott and Anantara. Sea turtles sometimes nest here from November to February. Patong is an hour away, and there is nothing to walk to at night.

      Stay here if you want a big resort on an empty beach close to the airport and do not plan many nights out.

      Karon

      Big, open beach with a relaxed small town

      beachswimmingfamiliesbudgetsunset

      A wide 3 km beach with a road and promenade behind it, so it never feels crowded. Most hotels are across the road, and the small town has beer bars, live music and good-value restaurants. Families and repeat visitors like it. The dry sand squeaks under your feet. Patong is about 15 minutes north and Kata is next door.

      Stay here if you want a big, calm beach and good value, with Patong's clubs about 15 minutes away.

      Kata (Kata Yai)

      Beautiful bay with an island; busy, easy and walkable

      beachswimmingfamiliesfoodsunset

      One of Phuket's most beautiful beaches, with soft sand, blue water and Koh Pu, a small island in the bay. It is busy, but nightlife is calm: beer bars, a night market and sunset bars. Club Med fills about 90% of the beachfront, so you reach the sand from the two ends. Many restaurants and hotels, from budget to luxury.

      Stay here if the beach matters most and you want an easy, walkable area with many restaurants.

      Kata Noi

      Small, clear bay shared by only three resorts

      beachswimmingcouplesquietsunset

      An 850 m bay just south of Kata, behind a rocky headland. Only three resorts share it (Katathani, The Shore and Mom Tri's Villa Royale), so it stays calm. There is no town; Kata's restaurants are a short ride away. The hill road above has sunset bars with a view of the bay: After Beach Bar, The Sundeck and Fira.

      Stay here if you want a calm, beautiful swimming beach and sunset bars, and do not need nightlife.

      Nai Harn

      Green hills, a lake and a protected beach in the south

      beachswimmingnaturesunsetlong stay

      A wide, soft beach between green hills, with a lake and a temple behind it and yachts in the bay. By law nothing can be built on the land behind the sand, so there are only tall casuarina trees. No town, just scattered restaurants, cafes and villas, with many long-stay expats. Busy in Dec-Jan, but relaxed.

      Stay here if you want nature, a great beach and a calm long-stay feel, and do not mind 30 minutes to Patong.

      Rawai, Ya Nui & Promthep

      Seafood, island boats and the famous sunset cape

      foodlocal lifelong staymuay thaisunsetsnorkeling

      The working harbour at Phuket's southern tip, not a swimming beach: longtail boats line the shore. People come for the seafood market (buy fish, a restaurant cooks it), boats to Koh Bon, Coral Island and Racha, and a slow local pace with expats, cafes and Muay Thai gyms. Ya Nui and Promthep Cape are a few minutes west.

      Stay here if you want a low-cost long-stay base with seafood, gyms and island boats, and will drive to swim.

      Chalong & Soi Ta-iad

      Fitness street, big temples and the island-boat pier

      muay thaiwellnesslong stayculturelocal life

      A local area on Chalong Bay, but with no swimming beach. Soi Ta-iad is Phuket's 'fitness street': 1.5 km of Muay Thai and MMA camps (Tiger Muay Thai since 2003), gyms, healthy cafes and long-stay rooms. Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha are close, and many island trips leave from Chalong Pier. You need a scooter or Grab.

      Stay here if you come to train, want long-stay prices and do not need a beach at your door.

      Phuket Town (Old Town)

      Old shophouses, the best food and real local life

      culturefoodlocal lifebudgetshopping

      Phuket's capital, a great half-day trip. The Old Town has restored Sino-Portuguese shophouses, Chinese shrines, street art, cafes and some of the best food on the island. Hotels are cheap. Bars are small and relaxed; Courage Bar hosted underground nights in Dec 2025-Feb 2026. The coast is 20-30 minutes away.

      Stay here if you love food, culture and low prices, and are happy to ride 30 minutes to the beach and the big clubs.

      Kathu

      Local food and jungle fun between Patong and town

      local lifefoodbudgetnaturelong stay

      The inland centre of the island, between Patong and Phuket Town. Most visitors drive through, but locals come for the food: Krua Jongjit is in the Michelin Guide, and dim sum breakfasts are cheap. Kathu Shrine is said to be where the Vegetarian Festival began. Golf, a water park, zip-lines and a wake park are here too.

      Stay here if you want low prices and real local food close to Patong, and do not need a sea view.

      Cape Panwa

      Quiet south-east cape with calm bays and a rooftop sunset

      quietcouplessunsetfamiliesnature

      A green, hilly cape in the south-east, about 20 minutes from Phuket Town. It is quiet: a few resorts, small bays such as Panwa Beach and Ao Yon, small beach restaurants and almost no nightlife. Phuket Aquarium is at the tip. Sri Panwa, the group behind Baba Beach Club, has its resort and the Baba Nest rooftop bar here.

      Stay here if you want peace, calm water and a short drive to Phuket Town, and do not mind an hour to the airport.

      Ao Po & Cape Yamu

      Marinas, luxury villas and boats to Koh Yao

      luxuryquietnaturecouples

      The quiet north-east coast, facing the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay. Ao Po Grand Marina has yachts, charters and resort boats to Koh Yao Noi (about 40 minutes); public speedboats leave from Bang Rong Pier nearby. Cape Yamu, to the south, has luxury villas and COMO Point Yamu. Almost no shops or nightlife.

      Stay here if you want a private luxury villa with Phang Nga Bay views and easy boats to Koh Yao, not a beach holiday.

      Thalang

      Heritage town, rainforest park and the local DJ scene

      culturenaturelocal lifebudgetairport

      The inland north, the island's historic heart, near the airport. Wat Phra Thong, the Heroines Monument and the Thalang National Museum tell Phuket's history. To the east, Khao Phra Thaeo forest has Bang Pae waterfall, a gibbon project and an elephant sanctuary. Enthusiast Place, a DJ studio, is near Bang Tao.

      Stay here if you want cheap, local and close to the airport, and you will drive to the beach and to parties.

      Natai & Khao Pilai (Phang Nga)

      Empty beach, Baba Beach Club and Circoloco Saturdays

      technobeach clubsbeachquietluxurycouplesairport

      About 10 km of wide, pale sand on the mainland north of the Sarasin Bridge, 35 minutes from the airport. No vendors, sunbeds or jet skis, and only a few resorts, most of them luxury. Baba Beach Club has a Funktion-One sound system and hosts Circoloco on Sat 9 and Sat 16 Jan, 15:00-03:00. You need a car or Grab.

      Stay here if you find a room: on the Circoloco Saturdays (9, 16 and 23 Jan) rooms are sold out or very expensive, so this guide suggests Kamala and a driver.

                                                  Baht ฿ · exchange · ATMs

                                                  Money

                                                  Bring clean USD or EUR 100 notes and change them at a money changer, not at the airport or the hotel. ATMs charge 250 to 350 baht (≈2,700 to 3,800 AMD) for each withdrawal.

                                                  Best place to change money
                                                  Mamy Exchange

                                                  Mamy Exchange

                                                  The best rate we could check is at Mamy Exchange in Koh Kaew, on route 402 between the airport and Phuket Town. On 15 Oct 2026 it paid 33.35 THB per USD 100 note and 37.35 THB per euro, about 0.5% under the mid-market rate. In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon. In Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (closed Sundays). Bank booths paid 0.4-1.2% less. ATMs charge 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD) (Visa) or 350 THB (≈3,800 AMD) (Mastercard) per withdrawal, so bring clean USD or EUR notes.

                                                  Airport banking and exchange info ↗

                                                  ATMs

                                                  In 2026 Thai bank ATMs charge foreign cards 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD) per withdrawal with Visa or UnionPay and 350 THB (≈3,800 AMD) with Mastercard (official fee tables: Kasikorn from 25 Aug 2026, SCB from 1 Sep 2026, Krungsri from 11 Mar 2026). Your home bank may add a fee. One withdrawal is usually 20,000-30,000 THB (≈216,000-324,000 AMD) at most.

                                                  Cheapest: We found no cheaper bank ATM: Kasikorn, SCB and Krungsri all charge 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD) (Visa) or 350 THB (≈3,800 AMD) (Mastercard). A 2026 guide says Bangkok Bank and Krungthai also charge 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD).; Use a Visa card if you have one. It saves 100 THB (≈1,100 AMD) on each withdrawal.; Take out the maximum each time (20,000-30,000 THB, ≈216,000-324,000 AMD). A 250 THB (≈2,700 AMD) fee is 1.25% of 20,000 THB (≈216,000 AMD) but 5% of 5,000 THB (≈54,000 AMD).; Use ATMs at bank branches or inside malls (Jungceylon, Central Festival). If the machine keeps your card, the bank can help.

                                                  • If the ATM offers to convert to your home currency, press 'Decline' or 'Without conversion'. Your own bank then converts at a better rate.
                                                  • Check the fee on the screen before you press OK.
                                                  • Wise and Revolut cards do not remove the Thai ATM fee of 250/350 THB (≈2,700/3,800 AMD).
                                                  • Standalone ATMs in bars and small shops can have lower withdrawal limits.
                                                  • Withdraw in daylight, cover your PIN, and keep your cash in two places.

                                                  Cards

                                                  • Always pay in THB. If a card machine offers your home currency (DCC), say no. On 15 Oct 2026 SCB's card DCC rate was 31.85 THB per USD, while the mid-market rate was 33.50. That is about 5% worse.
                                                  • Wise and Revolut cards convert close to the mid-market rate. Use them in malls, hotels, for Grab and for bigger bills.
                                                  • Revolut: do big exchanges on weekdays. Standard plans add about 1% at weekends. Check the free monthly limit of your plan.
                                                  • You still need cash for taxis, tuk-tuks, markets, beach bars and many small shops. Some places add a fee (often about 3%) for card payments.
                                                  • Bring two cards from different banks, ideally one Visa and one Mastercard. Keep one card in the hotel safe.
                                                  • Turn on foreign use in your banking app before you fly.

                                                  Tips

                                                  • Best plan: bring clean USD 100 or EUR 100/200 notes and change them at Mamy, Lion or the SuperRich partner. Use ATMs only as a backup.
                                                  • Big notes get better rates. At Mamy on 15 Oct 2026: USD 50-100 notes 33.35, USD 5-20 notes 33.05 and USD 1-2 notes 32.55 THB.
                                                  • Notes must be clean: not torn, not written on and not stamped. Old USD 100s get less: on 15 Oct 2026 Ex24 paid 33.08 for old 100s and 33.18 for new ones. Very old or damaged notes can be refused.
                                                  • Bring your original passport. Changers ask for it and write down the number. Count the baht at the counter and keep the receipt.
                                                  • Test a rate quickly: for USD 100 notes a good rate is within about 0.5% of the mid-market rate. On 15 Oct 2026 Mamy paid 33.35 when the mid-market rate was 33.50. A booth that pays 33.00 or less is about 1.5% under the mid-market rate.
                                                  • For USD 1,000 on 15 Oct 2026 you got 33,350 THB (≈360,000 AMD) at Mamy, 33,220 THB (≈359,000 AMD) at the ttb bank, 33,070 THB (≈357,000 AMD) at the SCB bank, and only about 31,850 THB (≈344,000 AMD) when you paid by card with DCC.
                                                  • When you arrive, change only a little at the airport or use an ATM there. Mamy is on Thepkrasattri Rd (route 402), on the way from the airport to Phuket Town and Patong. Ask your driver to stop (open Mon-Fri until 17:00, at weekends until 16:30).
                                                  • In Patong, use Lion in Jungceylon (09:00-21:00). Late at night, the Value Plus booth on Soi Sansabai is open until 04:00.
                                                  • In Phuket Old Town, use the SuperRich partner at Suriyadej Circle (Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00) or NC Plus (Mon-Sat). Both are closed on Sunday, and 10 Jan and 17 Jan 2027 are Sundays.
                                                  • In Kata/Karon, Rawai/Nai Harn and Bang Tao/Laguna, use Money Shop, Value Plus or a bank booth. Before you change a big amount, compare with Mamy's live rate on mamyexchange.com.
                                                  • Natai and Khao Pilai (Phang Nga) have almost no money changers (OpenStreetMap shows none). Bring baht from Phuket.
                                                  • Green SuperRich Thailand and Vasu Exchange have no Phuket branch: green SuperRich lists only Bangkok and nearby cities, and Vasu has one Bangkok office. The Google pin 'Superrich Money Exchange' on Wirat Hong Yok Rd is not SuperRich: the company there is registered as 'Sunrich Money Exchange'.
                                                  • On 15 Oct 2026 SuperRich in Bangkok paid 33.43-33.45 for a USD 100 note. Mamy in Phuket paid only about 0.1 THB less.
                                                  • If you leave the airport in Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi), SuperRich (green and orange) and Value Plus have booths on the B floor by the Airport Rail Link.
                                                  • Ask for some 100 and 500 baht (≈5,400 AMD) notes. Taxis and small shops often cannot change 1,000 baht (≈10,800 AMD) notes.
                                                  • Changing baht back at a good changer costs little (Mamy sold USD at 33.50 on 15 Oct 2026), but don't change much more than you need.
                                                  • No Thai bank holiday falls on your dates (8-26 Jan 2027): the only bank holiday in January 2027 is 1 Jan. Some Phuket Town changers close on Sundays (10, 17 and 24 Jan).

                                                  Avoid

                                                  • Hotel reception exchange desks: rates are usually much worse.
                                                  • Airport counters for big amounts: local guides estimate 3-5% worse than town.
                                                  • Saying yes to your home currency (DCC) at an ATM or card machine: about 5% worse.
                                                  • Many small ATM withdrawals: you pay 250-350 THB (≈2,700-3,800 AMD) each time.
                                                  • Bank booths when a top changer is near: on 15 Oct 2026 they paid 0.4-0.8% less for USD and about 1-1.2% less for EUR.
                                                  • Street booths with a 'No commission' sign but a low rate. Compare the board with the mid-market rate first.
                                                  • Strangers or Telegram accounts that offer exchange or cash delivery. Mamy says it has no Telegram account, and Money Shop names two fake Telegram accounts.
                                                  • Changing small, old or damaged notes.
                                                  • Shops that use the SuperRich name but are not on the official superrich1965.com list.
